patterns.context: Concerns banks, credit scores, and payday loan services, but the sentences themselves contain obvious concatenation or semantic anomalies.

patterns.name: Marketing language about prices and improving life
patterns.context: First emphasizes affordability, then markets content through a question and a promise of life improvement.
patterns.domain: Web advertisements or low-quality marketing copy

patterns.name: Emotion and everyday descriptions in poetry
patterns.context: Verse expresses hope, disappointment, and sorrow, and describes everyday farm tasks.

patterns.name: Neurotechnology and veterans' health
patterns.context: Introduces technologies and therapies that help veterans with nervous system disorders recover function; subsequent text also contains tokenization anomalies.

patterns.name: Historical narrative and economics textbook fragments
patterns.context: The same passage concatenates a historical narrative about the American Civil War with economics text about consumption, investment, and human capital.
patterns.domain: Web encyclopedia-style history and economics textbook text

9_2056.description: 激活分散于碎裂子词、异常 token 与普通词，也出现在农业、教育、金融、营销、诗歌、生物医学及历史经济文本；没有跨段稳定的语义或句法模式。

patterns.name: 伪词边界处的分词片段
patterns.context: 激活落在单词内部的子词或被切分的词段上，常伴随相邻片段也有激活；不要求固定语义上下文。
patterns.domain: 混合语料、技术文本及乱码或异常分词文本

patterns.name: 稀有或异常 token 序列
patterns.context: token 序列明显碎裂，含非英语字符、零散字母、空白或标点；难以从连贯语义解释激活。
patterns.domain: EuroParl 文本与法律文档抽取/格式噪声

patterns.name: 功能词及常见词的局部激活
patterns.context: 常见词在各自语境中零星激活，未见稳定的句法位置或语义条件。
patterns.domain: 混合网页、散文与机构文本

patterns.name: 科学与工程术语周边
patterns.context: 出现在涉及遗传工程、科学价值或空气动力学的混杂网页文本中；激活集中在术语及其邻近词，但上下文噪声较大。
patterns.domain: 网页文本、科学/工程相关内容

patterns.name: 植物育种性状及方法
patterns.context: 谈及作物性状、抗性、农艺品质，以及育种或选择方法。
patterns.domain: 专利背景技术、农业生物技术

patterns.name: 姓名识别与个性化学习
patterns.context: 介绍个性化学习，并称每位学生都以姓名为人所知。

patterns.name: 银行与贷款查询的混杂文本
patterns.context: 围绕银行、信用评分及发薪日贷款服务展开，但句子本身存在明显拼接或语义异常。
patterns.domain: 网页文本、金融相关内容

patterns.name: 价格与生活改善营销话术
patterns.context: 先强调价格实惠，再以提问和承诺生活改善的方式推销内容。
patterns.domain: 网页广告或低质量营销文案

patterns.name: 诗歌中的情绪与日常描写
patterns.context: 韵文表达希望、失望与忧愁，并描写农场日常事务。

patterns.name: 神经科技与退伍军人健康
patterns.context: 介绍帮助神经系统障碍退伍军人恢复功能的技术与疗法；后续文字也有分词异常。
patterns.domain: NIH 项目摘要、生物医学

patterns.name: 历史叙述与经济学章节片段
patterns.context: 同一段拼接了南北战争相关历史叙述和关于消费、投资及人力资本的经济学文本。
patterns.domain: 网页百科式历史与经济学教材文本

en.description: Responses are distributed across the English words are and Each, several Spanish or multilingual word fragments, and various short English words and subwords within words; the passages differ markedly in domain, syntax, and semantics, with no stable unified theme.

patterns.name: English are
patterns.context: The standalone English word are appears; no fixed sentence pattern is required, and surrounding content varies.
patterns.domain: Emails, NIH project texts, web questions

patterns.name: English Each
patterns.context: Each is followed by a noun phrase to make an individual statement or describe personalized education.

patterns.name: Spanish word-ending sequences
patterns.context: Spanish words are split into multiple subword tokens in sentences about traffic and monetization.

patterns.name: Specific subwords in names/common-word segmentation
patterns.context: Activations fall on subwords within words or on word subword tokens; they appear respectively in a person's name, an Italian number name, and an English number word.

patterns.name: Sporadic responses on short English words or subwords within words
patterns.context: High-frequency function words in different syntactic positions, or short subwords segmented from words; no stable collocations or consistent semantics.
patterns.domain: Scientific abstracts, emails, political commentary, economics texts, NIH and patent texts

patterns.name: Occasional activations on tokens within long words
patterns.context: Activations occur on fragments within words after they have been split into multiple tokens; the word meanings and domains are not consistent.

patterns.name: Fragments without a unified explanation
patterns.context: The short contexts provided are insufficient to determine whether they arise from word fragments, formatting, or incidental responses.
patterns.domain: Patent background texts and mixed corpora

9_2056.description: 响应分散在英语 are、Each、若干西班牙语或多语词片段及多种英语短词和词内子词上；各段领域、句法与语义差异明显，未见稳定统一主题。

patterns.name: 英语 are
patterns.context: 英语中出现独立词 are；不要求固定句型，前后内容各异
patterns.domain: 邮件、NIH 项目文本、网页问句

patterns.name: 英语 Each
patterns.context: Each 后接名词短语，用于逐一陈述或个性化教育描述

patterns.name: 西班牙语词尾序列
patterns.context: 西班牙语词被分成多个子词 token，出现在关于访问量及变现的句子中

patterns.name: 专名/普通词切分中的特定子词
patterns.context: 激活落在词内部或词的子词 token 上；分别出现在人名、意大利语数字名称、英文数字词中
patterns.domain: 百科条目、NIH 项目文本

patterns.name: 英文短词或词内子词的零散响应
patterns.context: 不同句法位置中的高频功能词，或被切分出来的短子词；没有稳定搭配或一致语义
patterns.domain: 科学摘要、邮件、政治评论、经济学文本、NIH 与专利文本

patterns.name: 长词内部 token 的偶发激活
patterns.context: 激活出现在词被拆成多个 token 后的词内片段，所涉词义和领域不统一

patterns.name: 无法统一解释的片段
patterns.context: 仅凭所给短上下文难以判定其是否来自词片段、格式或偶然响应
patterns.domain: 专利背景文本及混杂语料

en.description: Activation is scattered across specific subword fragments in various words, sentence-initial phrases, and structures adjacent to numbers; clearer local repetitions include “When we,” Derelict, and Root/Roots. Most other instances are isolated fragments that are difficult to group into a unified semantic or domain pattern.

patterns.name: Word-final fragments in pseudowords
patterns.context: Activation falls on segmented English word fragments; both occurrences are in concatenated or unnatural text, with no consistent lexical condition apparent.
patterns.domain: Web text, noisy or corrupted text

patterns.name: Sentence-initial “When we”
patterns.context: Sentences begin with When we, followed by a past-tense verb; one concerns research groups and the other dating arrangements.

patterns.name: Initial or internal “De” fragment
patterns.context: The same word, “Derelict,” recurs in an entry title, with activation distributed over its tokenized fragments.

patterns.name: Root/Roots
patterns.context: Root/Roots appears in isolated title or entry fragments; capitalization and prefixes vary.

patterns.name: PCB “Pads”
patterns.context: Pads refers to exposed solder pads on a printed circuit board; activation is concentrated in the latter part of the word.

patterns.name: Sentence-initial “Of course”
patterns.context: A quotation begins with Of course to introduce a concession or additional explanation, discussing amenities.
patterns.domain: Commentary on household tasks and technology

patterns.name: Consecutive determiners and numbers
patterns.context: An economics discussion contains words such as period and generation, along with adjacent numbers and Each.

patterns.name: Basic question sentence
patterns.context: In a discussion of political beliefs, how do we introduces an explanatory question.

patterns.name: Other scattered activations
patterns.context: Occur separately in unnatural web fragments, bank-loan-related text, and discussion of household conveniences; no stable shared lexical or syntactic condition is apparent.
patterns.domain: Web text, finance-related text, commentary on domestic life

9_2056.description: 激活分散于多个词的特定子词片段、句首短语及数字邻接结构；较清楚的局部重复包括“When we”、Derelict、Root/Roots。其余多为孤立片段，难以归为统一语义或领域模式。

patterns.name: 伪词中的词尾片段
patterns.context: 激活落在被切分的英文词片段中；两处都处于拼接或不自然文本，未显现一致的词义条件。
patterns.domain: 网页文本、噪声或乱码文本

patterns.name: 句首「When we」
patterns.context: 句首以 When we 起始，后接过去式动词；一个涉及研究分组，另一个涉及约会安排。

patterns.name: 词首或词内「De」片段
patterns.context: 词条标题中反复出现同一个词「Derelict」，激活分布在其分词片段上。

patterns.name: 词根「Root/Roots」
patterns.context: 孤立的标题或词条片段中出现 Root/Roots；大小写和前缀不同。

patterns.name: PCB「Pads」
patterns.context: Pads 指印刷电路板上设置并暴露的焊盘；激活集中在词的后半部分。

patterns.name: 句首「Of course」
patterns.context: 引号内以 Of course 引出让步或补充说明，谈便利设施。
patterns.domain: 关于家务与技术的评论文字

patterns.name: 连续限定词与数字
patterns.trigger: 「In»4« every»6« period»4« t»4« a»8« generation」及「4»5« Each»6« member」
patterns.context: 经济学论述中出现 period、generation 等词，以及紧邻的数字和 Each。

patterns.name: 基础性问题句
patterns.context: 谈政治信念时，以 how do we 引出解释性问题。

patterns.name: 其他分散激活
patterns.context: 分别出现在不自然的网页片段、银行贷款相关文本及家务便利话题中；未见稳定共享的词义或句法条件。
patterns.domain: 网页文本、金融相关文本、家庭生活评论

en.description: Activations often fall on within-word or cross-tokenization fragments, especially re and segmented words; they also extend across ordinary whole words, French fragments, and forum fragments, making it difficult to identify a stable semantic or syntactic pattern.

patterns.name: Cross-word fragment “re”
patterns.context: Activations cluster on “re” between adjacent fragments: [5] is «Me»«re» Raj«a», as if a word were segmented; [7] is «it»«re»«?», likewise a combination of adjacent fragments.

patterns.name: Within-word fragments split across lines
patterns.context: Activations fall on parts of words segmented by tokenization or line breaks, at varying positions within words; examples include middle or initial segments and line-break splits.
patterns.domain: Legal texts, NIH project descriptions, medical papers, and abstracts

patterns.name: Scattered word fragments in general English contexts
patterns.context: In general English sentences, concatenated text, or questions, multiple whole words and word fragments activate; there is no clear, stable lexical or syntactic condition.

patterns.name: Within-word fragments in French
patterns.context: Activations fall on a within-word fragment of a French adjective; other French words in the passage have mostly weaker activations.

patterns.name: Trailing fragment in forum text
patterns.context: Appears in a quoted or truncated conversation fragment at the end of a post, “all we in”; there is no obvious semantic trigger condition.

9_2056.concept: 对词片段的非特异性响应
9_2056.description: 激活多落在词内或跨分词片段上，尤其是 re 及被拆分的词；但也分散覆盖普通完整词、法语片段和论坛片段，难以归结为稳定语义或句法模式。

patterns.name: 跨词片段「re」
patterns.context: 激活集中在紧邻前后片段的「re」上：[5] 为 «Me»«re» Raj«a»，像是词被切分；[7] 为 «it»«re»«?»，同样是相邻片段组合。
patterns.domain: Wikipedia 标题/碎片；数学题文本

patterns.name: 跨行切分出的词内片段
patterns.context: 激活落在词被分词或换行拆开的部分上，词内位置不固定；可见于单词中段、前段或跨行拆分。
patterns.domain: 法律、NIH 项目描述、医学论文及摘要

patterns.name: 一般英文语境中的分散词片段
patterns.context: 在一般英文句子、拼接文本或提问中，对多个完整词及词片段都有激活；没有清晰稳定的词义或句法条件。

patterns.name: 法语词内片段
patterns.context: 激活落在法语形容词的词内片段；该段其他法语词多为较弱激活。

patterns.name: 论坛文本中的尾部片段
patterns.context: 出现在帖子末尾引用或截断的对话片段“all we in”；没有明显语义触发条件。

en.concept: Local word forms and fragment detection
en.description: Activations are dispersed across domains: common words, subwords, and punctuation can all trigger them. Several passages contain words following an, and others involve finance, medicine, literature, catalogs, and code; no unified semantic regularity is evident.

patterns.name: Elements following a in a sentence
patterns.context: Activations cluster on the word following the indefinite article an; they sometimes also appear near a, the, or other local collocations, but inconsistently.
patterns.domain: Multiple genres; not attributable to a single domain

patterns.name: Common words and fragments within phrases
patterns.context: Many ordinary words, punctuation marks, and within-word fragments are marked in one passage, with little apparent semantic or syntactic selectivity.

patterns.name: Financial distress context
patterns.context: Involves installment loans, financial hardship, and credit products; activations are scattered across multiple words and subwords.

patterns.name: Rare or elderly populations
patterns.context: Describes study participants as rare or elderly populations; there is no clear, stable lexical trigger.

patterns.name: Influencer relationships
patterns.context: Discusses the influence of influencers and the basis of their relationships.

patterns.name: Medical device phrase
patterns.context: Experience with an ultrasound stethoscope; activations span fragments within Experience and neighboring words.

patterns.name: Grotesque literary-style wording
patterns.context: Incoherent narration with a grotesque or absurd quality, in which multiple rare words and subwords are marked.

patterns.name: Abstract critical statement
patterns.context: Discusses the phenomenal world and criticism; activations cluster on fragments within barren and near an article phrase.

patterns.name: Transparent, luminous, foldable object
patterns.context: Describes an object as transparent, photoluminescent, and foldable; activations occur across several adjacent words.

patterns.name: Book table-of-contents titles
patterns.context: Uppercase book titles, authors, volume numbers, and table-of-contents section titles; words are split into irregular subwords.

patterns.name: GStreamer Equalizer identifier
patterns.context: The GstIirEqualizerNBands identifier and its segmented fragments recur in C code.

9_2056.description: 激活跨领域且分散：常见词、子词和标点均可触发；若干段落含 an 后词，也涉及金融、医学、文学、目录与代码等局部内容，未见统一语义规律。

patterns.name: 句中 a 后的成分
patterns.context: 激活集中在不定冠词 an 之后的下一个词；有时也出现在 a、the 或其他局部搭配附近，但不一致。
patterns.domain: 多种文体；不能归为单一领域

patterns.name: 常见词与短语内部片段
patterns.trigger: « n»4«'t»6« therapeutic»6« or»7« very»6« based»4«.»4« If»5« the»7« file»6« is»8«
patterns.context: 一段中大量普通词、标点及词内片段都被标记，缺少明显的语义或句法选择性。

patterns.name: 金融困境语境
patterns.trigger: « financial»2« difficulty»2« pay»2«day»3« loans»3« ... ris«3qu« persuade»8
patterns.context: 涉及分期贷款、财务困难及信贷产品；激活散落在多个词和子词上。

patterns.name: 稀有或高龄人群
patterns.context: 描述研究对象为罕见、年长的人群；无清晰稳定的词汇触发点。

patterns.name: 影响者关系
patterns.trigger: «The»1« power»6« of»5« an»8« influ«3«encer»2« resides»2« in»4« a»5« meaningful»4« relationship»1
patterns.context: 讨论影响者的影响力及其关系基础。

patterns.name: 医学器械短语
patterns.context: 超声听诊器相关经历；激活覆盖 Experience 的词内片段和邻近词。

patterns.name: 怪诞文学式措辞
patterns.context: 不连贯、带有怪诞或荒诞感的叙述，多个罕见词及子词被标记。

patterns.name: 抽象批评语句
patterns.trigger: «The»1« bar»5«ren»7« prospect»5« of»6« a»8« representation»4« world»3
patterns.context: 谈论表象世界及批评；激活集中在 barren 的词内片段和冠词短语附近。

patterns.name: 透明发光可折叠物
patterns.trigger: «Let»1« it»3« shine»4«:»5« a»7« transparent»4« and»3« phot«1«ol»1«umines«2«cent»2« fold»3«able»1
patterns.context: 描述透明、光致发光、可折叠的物品；激活在多个相邻词上。

patterns.name: 书籍目录标题
patterns.context: 大写书名、作者、卷号和目录章节标题；词被拆成不规则子词。

patterns.name: GStreamer Equalizer 标识符
patterns.context: C 代码中反复出现 GstIirEqualizerNBands 标识符及其拆分片段。

en.concept: Local English word-form and syntactic cues
en.description: Responses are relatively consistent for sentence-initial “When” and local “an” collocations, and also activate several segmented words and a proper name; the remaining scattered words are difficult to group into a common pattern.

patterns.name: Conditional sentences beginning with when
patterns.context: A sentence begins with “When” to introduce a condition, time, or research context, followed by a subject and predicate; this is clear in all three passages.

patterns.name: Local collocations with the English article an
patterns.context: The article an appears before a noun phrase; its position and collocation vary, and some contexts are not sentence-initial.

patterns.name: Irregular tokenization or within-word segmentation
patterns.context: Words are split into multiple tokens, or local word fragments are marked; there is no shared meaning or fixed word form.
patterns.domain: Mixed; general prose, medical texts, and academic texts

patterns.name: Proper name Mere Raja
patterns.context: The name is split into multiple subwords and repeated in adjacent lines.

patterns.name: Scattered local word activations
patterns.context: Isolated words or subwords activate in each passage, with no stable syntactic, semantic, or stylistic condition.

9_2056.concept: 英文局部词形与句式线索
9_2056.description: 较稳定地响应句首“When”及局部“an”搭配，也会激活若干被拆分的词和一个专名；其余零散词语难以归为共同模式。

patterns.name: when 开头的条件句
patterns.context: 句首以“When”引出条件、时间或研究情境，后接主语和谓语；在三段中均明显。
patterns.domain: 科学论文、邮件、专利背景

patterns.name: 英文冠词 an 的局部搭配
patterns.context: 冠词 an 出现在名词短语前；触发位置和搭配内容不同，部分上下文并非句首。

patterns.name: 不规则分词或词内切分
patterns.context: 词被拆成多个 token，或单词局部片段被标记；没有共同的词义或固定词形。
patterns.domain: 混合；一般散文、医学文本及学术文本

patterns.name: 专名 Mere Raja
patterns.context: 名称被切分成多个子词，并在相邻行中重复。

patterns.name: 零散的局部词语激活
patterns.context: 各段中出现孤立的词或子词激活，未显示稳定的句法、语义或文体条件。
patterns.domain: 网页文本、散文、语言学文本

en.description: Activation is dispersed across segments, focusing on common words, title words, and internal subwords, including nearly, an, the, We, Each, and EVERY. Although several text types can be identified, no stable semantic or grammatical condition is apparent.

patterns.name: Random internal subwords and tokenization boundaries
patterns.context: Trigger positions are scattered, often within common words, at sentence beginnings, or on internal subwords; there is no stable local semantic condition across segments
patterns.domain: Cross-corpus and cross-genre; may involve word fragments or common words, but evidence is insufficient to establish a specific pattern

patterns.name: Biomedical abstract fragment
patterns.context: Appears in the opening phrase «Experience with an ultrasound stethoscope.»

patterns.name: EVERY in a title or proper name
patterns.context: Appears in the all-caps title/lyrics «THE PATH OF EVERYONE», the album name «Every Band Has...», or educational copy «Each student...»; capitalization and following words vary
patterns.domain: Music catalogs, educational promotion, title text

patterns.name: Sentence-initial We
patterns.context: Appears in the title «How We Do It», followed by a line break and another passage

patterns.name: Group in a category or organization name
patterns.context: Immediately follows a Q&A marker and line break, followed by «/organize program icons and files»

patterns.name: Common words in financial advertising
patterns.context: Appears in loan promotional copy, but these words also occur in other segments, so finance-specific semantic activation cannot be established

patterns.name: Scattered words in a neurotechnology project description
patterns.context: Appears at the end of a description of a nervous-system therapy project for veterans; there is no stable evidence of specialized terminology triggering activation

patterns.name: Scattered words in catalogs/abstracts
patterns.context: Appears in biology abstracts, journal information, and keyword fragments; the relationship between trigger words and topic is unclear

9_2056.description: 激活散布于各段，集中在常见词、标题词及词内子词，包含 nearly、an、the、We、Each、EVERY 等；虽可列出若干文体片段，但看不出稳定语义或语法条件。

patterns.name: 随机内部子词与分词边界
patterns.trigger: 如 «nearly»、«in»、«an»、«the»、«should»、«Each»、«We»、«every»、«Focus»、«Group»；多处激活落在词的一部分，如 «EX»、«ML»、«Shared»?（原文 « shared»）、«cal»、«velop»、«trans»、«Experience» 中的 «ience»
patterns.context: 触发位置分散，常位于常见词、句首或词内子词；各段间没有稳定一致的局部语义条件
patterns.domain: 跨语料、跨文体；可能涉及词片段或常见词，但证据不足以确立具体模式

patterns.name: 生物医学摘要片段
patterns.context: 出现在摘要开头短语 «Experience with an ultrasound stethoscope.» 中

patterns.name: 标题或专名中的 EVERY
patterns.context: 出现在大写标题/歌词 «THE PATH OF EVERYONE»、专辑名 «Every Band Has...»，或教育文案 «Each student...»；大小写和后续词各异
patterns.domain: 音乐目录、教育宣传、标题文本

patterns.name: 句首 We
patterns.context: 出现在标题 «How We Do It» 中，之后接换行和另一段文字

patterns.name: 栏目或组织名中的 Group
patterns.context: 紧接问答标记与换行，后接 «/organize program icons and files»

patterns.name: 金融广告常见词
patterns.context: 出现在借贷宣传文案，但这些词也在其他段出现，无法证明是金融语义特异反应

patterns.name: 神经科技项目描述中的零散词
patterns.context: 出现在面向退伍军人的神经系统疗法项目描述末尾；没有稳定的专业术语触发证据

patterns.name: 目录/摘要中的零散词
patterns.context: 出现在生物学摘要、期刊信息和关键词碎片中，触发词与主题的对应关系不明确
patterns.domain: 生物医学及文献目录文本

en.description: Activations are scattered: several maxima fall on initial word fragments after an or on subsequent words, and our also occurs; other examples involve educational phrases, slash-separated terms in Q&A, an email puzzle, WPAD code, cancer targets, and noisy text, with no unified semantic pattern.

patterns.name: Initial tokens after the article an
patterns.context: The strongest activations often occur on the initial fragment of the word immediately following an, such as «Stud» and «Exper»; they also occur on complete words or their initial fragments after an. In different contexts, our receives the highest activation, indicating that the trigger condition is not entirely consistent.
patterns.domain: Research abstracts, medicine/health, business emails, and general web text

patterns.name: Personalized learning phrase
patterns.context: Personalized Learning is followed by text about students and educational institutions.

patterns.name: Slash in Q&A text
patterns.context: After the Q&A-format opening, the body contains an operational phrase joined by a slash.

patterns.name: Email puzzle wording
patterns.context: Begins with This week and poses a mystery to solve.

patterns.name: WPAD code comments
patterns.context: Python HTTP client code and comments discuss WPAD hosts and request paths.

patterns.name: Target and cancer language
patterns.context: An abstract-style statement of objectives is followed by a reduction in cancer-related morbidity and mortality.

patterns.name: Noisy or anomalously concatenated text
patterns.context: The sentence has incoherent semantics and collocations, with anomalous word fragments and concatenated text; it is difficult to attribute to a single clear trigger condition.

9_2056.description: 激活分散：多个最高值落在 an 后的词首片段或后续词上，也有 our；其余涉及教育短语、问答斜杠词组、邮件谜题、WPAD代码、癌症目标及噪声文本，未见统一语义模式。

patterns.name: 冠词 an 后的词首 token
patterns.context: 最强激活多出现在 an 后紧接的词首片段，如 «Stud»、«Exper»；也出现在 an 后的完整词或其首片段。不同上下文中还有 our 获得最高激活，说明触发条件并不完全一致。
patterns.domain: 科研摘要、医学/健康、商业邮件及一般网络文本

patterns.name: 个人化学习短语
patterns.context: Personalized Learning 后接学生与教育机构相关表述。

patterns.name: 问答文本中的斜杠
patterns.context: 问答格式开头后，正文出现由斜杠连接的操作词组。

patterns.name: 邮件谜题用语
patterns.context: 以 This week 开头，提出一个待解的 mystery。

patterns.name: WPAD 代码注释
patterns.context: Python HTTP 客户端代码及注释中讨论 WPAD host 和请求路径。

patterns.name: 目标与癌症表述
patterns.context: 摘要式目标陈述，后接降低癌症相关发病率与死亡率。

patterns.name: 噪声或异常拼接文本
patterns.context: 句子语义与搭配不连贯，并夹杂异常词片段和拼接文本；难以归结为单一明确触发条件。

en.description: High activations often fall on English word-initial function words, subsequent within-word subwords, and abbreviations or nearby punctuation; the material spans emails, abstracts, Q&A, and web titles. Several domain-specific phrases appear only once and are difficult to group under a unified semantic trigger.

patterns.name: Unstressed function words at word beginnings
patterns.context: In continuous English text, function words often occur before content words or phrases; activations fall on word-initial/subword fragments rather than being distributed uniformly across the whole word.

patterns.name: Within-word subword boundaries or stem continuations
patterns.context: In words split into multiple subwords, subsequent within-word fragments receive high activations; some examples also contain preceding function words.
patterns.domain: Education, medical abstracts, email promotional copy

patterns.name: Abbreviations/punctuation at the start of phrases
patterns.context: In email conventions, Q&A labels, or compounds/titles, activations occur near abbreviation punctuation, slashes, or hyphens.

patterns.name: Names and identity expressions
patterns.context: Personalized education wording such as “Each student ... known by name”; strong activations in this passage center on Each.

patterns.name: Medical device phrase
patterns.context: In “Experience with an ultrasound stethoscope,” the suffix within a word and the article are strong; there are no similar medical passages to confirm a medical-specific trigger.

patterns.name: Abbreviations in email imperatives
patterns.context: The contraction suffix stands out in email expressions such as “Let's not forget...” or “Let's make sure...”.

patterns.name: Numbered stages and proper-name fragments
patterns.context: An operational context contains a stage number followed by a proper name or truncated word; activations are scattered, and evidence for an independent regularity is limited.

patterns.name: Web navigation and title formatting
patterns.context: Navigation, subscription prompts, and holiday titles are mixed together, with line breaks and within-word segmentation.

patterns.name: Title-style course description
patterns.context: A short title or promotional phrase beginning with An easy to follow.

patterns.name: File organization terms in Q&A
patterns.context: The Q&A body discusses organizing program icons and files; the slash and a subword fragment of organization are prominent.

patterns.name: List arrangement in emails
patterns.context: An email phrasing for reminders or scheduling; it shares the Let's contraction with another email, but the subsequent semantics differ.

patterns.name: Wording about research on rare populations
patterns.context: An abstract opening about rare, aging populations; activations are mainly on within-word fragments and the article.

9_2056.concept: 英语子词与功能词片段
9_2056.description: 高激活常落在英语词首功能词、词内子词续段及缩写/标点附近；材料横跨邮件、摘要、问答和网页标题。另有若干仅出现一次的领域措辞，难以归为统一语义触发。

patterns.name: 词首的非重读功能词
patterns.context: 英语连续文本中，功能词常出现在内容词或短语之前；激活落在词首/子词片段上，而非整个词均匀分布。

patterns.name: 词内子词边界或词干延续
patterns.context: 多子词切分的词中，词内后续片段获得较高激活；部分例子同时含有前置功能词。
patterns.domain: 教育、医学摘要、邮件宣传语

patterns.name: 短语开头的缩写/标点
patterns.context: 邮件惯用短语、问答标签或复合词/标题中，缩写标点、斜线或连字符附近激活。

patterns.name: 姓名与身份表达
patterns.context: “Each student ... known by name”这类个体化教育表述；本段强激活集中在 Each。

patterns.name: 医学器械短语
patterns.context: “Experience with an ultrasound stethoscope”中，词内后缀和冠词较强；没有同类医学段落可确认专属触发。

patterns.name: 邮件中的祈使句缩写
patterns.context: “Let's not forget...”或“Let's make sure...”邮件表达中，缩写后缀突出。

patterns.name: 数字阶段与专名片段
patterns.context: 运营语境中出现阶段编号及后续专名/截断词；激活较分散，独立规律证据有限。

patterns.name: 网页导航与标题排版
patterns.context: 导航、订阅提示与节日标题混排，含换行和词内切分。

patterns.name: 标题式课程描述
patterns.context: 以 An easy to follow 开头的简短标题/宣传语。

patterns.name: 问答中的文件整理术语
patterns.context: 问答正文讨论整理程序图标与文件，斜线和组织一词的子词片段显著。

patterns.name: 邮件中的列表安排
patterns.context: 提醒或安排事项的邮件句式；与另一封邮件共享 Let's 缩写，但后续语义不同。

patterns.name: 罕见人群研究措辞
patterns.context: 研究罕见、老龄化人群的摘要开头；激活主要在词内片段和冠词。

en.description: Activations occur on segmented word fragments, title words, names, and abbreviations across multiple types of text; code protocols and all-caps image captions also show independent high activations. No stable semantic theme is evident, and the examples cannot all be explained by shared word meanings.

patterns.name: Within-word segmentation and subword boundaries
patterns.context: Strong activations cluster on specific word fragments, especially near tokenization boundaries; sometimes they fall on a whole word or one token in a phrase. The word meanings are not consistent across passages.
patterns.domain: Across web, research abstracts, emails, forums, and other texts

patterns.name: Titles or title-like phrases
patterns.context: In title-style capitalization, phrases, or promotional copy, multiple common words and their fragments activate; there is no single trigger word consistent across passages.
patterns.domain: Web titles, HackerNews titles, or tutorial titles

patterns.name: Names, proper nouns, and segmented forms
patterns.context: Activations occur in segmented spellings of brands, products, organizations, proper nouns, or likely proper nouns; these instances vary considerably.
patterns.domain: Education webpages, medical abstracts, emails, web/image captions

patterns.name: Local activation on an at the start of a word
patterns.context: In two passages, «an» is a standalone token occurring mid-sentence, but the following words and semantics differ; this may reflect a local token trigger and does not establish a semantic condition.

patterns.name: Protocols and identifiers in code
patterns.context: Appears in code comments related to HTTP/WPAD and request-handling code; strong activations fall on segmented protocol or abbreviation character fragments.

patterns.name: All-caps, emphatic text
patterns.context: An image caption or promotional all-caps phrase following a line break, with words split into multiple fragments; the same passage also contains ordinary proper nouns and explanatory text.

patterns.name: Scattered title words and number expressions
patterns.context: Tutorial titles and income-number phrases contain several moderate activations, but lack semantic trigger conditions consistent with other passages.

9_2056.description: 激活分布在多类文本的拆分词片段、标题词、专名与缩写；代码协议、全大写图片说明等也有独立高激活。未见稳定语义主题，无法由共同词义解释全部例子。

patterns.name: 词内分段与词首续接
patterns.trigger: 词被拆成多个 token，如 «Personal»1«ized»7、«Exper»1«ience»9、«an»10« e»4«Spe»5«ak»6、«An»10«ad»5«ia»6；也包括 «To»10« Use»7
patterns.context: 强激活集中在词的特定片段，尤其是分词边界附近；有时落在完整词或短语的一个 token 上。各段具体词义并不统一。
patterns.domain: 跨网页、论文摘要、邮件、论坛及其他文本

patterns.name: 标题或标题式短语
patterns.context: 标题式大小写、短语或宣传语中，多个常见词及其片段激活；没有一个跨段一致的触发词。
patterns.domain: 网页标题、HackerNews 标题或教程标题

patterns.name: 名称、专名及拆分形式
patterns.context: 激活出现在品牌、产品、机构、专名或疑似专名的分段拼写中；这些实例彼此差异较大。
patterns.domain: 教育网页、医学摘要、邮件、网页/图片说明

patterns.name: 词首 an 的局部激活
patterns.trigger: «an»10（[3] 的«an»后接« e»«Spe»；[7] 的«an»后接 operational）
patterns.context: 两段中 «an» 都是独立 token 且处于句中，但后续词及语义不同，可能是局部 token 触发，不能据此确定语义条件。

patterns.name: 代码中的协议与标识符
patterns.context: 出现在 HTTP/WPAD 相关代码注释及请求处理代码中；强激活落在被拆开的协议或缩写字符片段。

patterns.name: 全大写、强调式文字
patterns.context: 换行后的图片说明或宣传式全大写短语，词被拆分成多个片段；同段也含普通专名与说明文字。
patterns.domain: 网页图片说明/新闻式文案

patterns.name: 零散标题词与数字表达
patterns.context: 教程标题及收入数字短语中有多处中等激活，但缺乏与其他段一致的语义触发条件。

en.description: Activation is distributed across internal fragments of multiple words and short words in various domains; it often occurs alongside capitalized titles, catalog formatting, or broken concatenated text. Trigger positions vary across segments, and no reliable single semantic or syntactic condition has been identified.

patterns.name: Initial fragments after tokenization
patterns.context: Activation often falls on internal English word fragments or subword fragments at the beginnings of adjacent words, especially short tokens such as «Each», «an», and «/»; it is not tied to a fixed complete word or semantic meaning.

patterns.name: Capitalized words at sentence openings or in titles
patterns.context: Strong activation appears near capitalized words, title words, or sentence-initial words, but the specific words and contexts vary considerably.
patterns.domain: Web, medical abstracts, Q&A, patents, and catalog text

patterns.name: Common short words in broken or corrupted text
patterns.context: Passages contain clear concatenation, disorder, or incoherence; activation focuses on high-frequency short words or local word fragments, with no stable topical condition apparent.

patterns.name: Catalog and numbering formats
patterns.context: Activation appears near tables of contents, chapter numbering, Roman numerals, and title formatting; it falls on different fragments, so it is unclear whether the format itself is the trigger.
patterns.domain: Book tables of contents and technical documents

patterns.name: Financial-word adjacency
patterns.context: A group of activations occurs near financial words such as loans, interest rates, and repayments, but the text is heavily fragmented, making it impossible to determine whether the trigger is financial semantics.

patterns.name: Clearly unrelated anomalous concatenations
patterns.context: Multiple unrelated fragments activate in text with semantic jumps, concatenated words, or apparent machine-generated/crawl noise.

9_2056.description: 激活分布在多领域、多个词内部片段及短词上；常伴标题大写、目录格式或破碎拼接文本。各段触发位置不一致，暂无可靠的单一语义或句法条件。

patterns.name: 分词后的词首片段
patterns.context: 激活常落在英语词的内部或相邻词首的子词片段上，尤其是「Each」「an」「/」等短 token；并非固定完整词或固定语义。

patterns.name: 句首或标题式大写词
patterns.context: 大写词、标题词或句首词附近出现较强激活，但具体词和语境差别很大。
patterns.domain: 网页、医学摘要、问答、专利及目录文本

patterns.name: 被破碎或乱码文本中的常见短词
patterns.context: 段落含有明显拼接、错乱或不连贯文本；激活集中在高频短词或局部词片段，未见稳定主题条件。

patterns.name: 目录与编号格式
patterns.trigger: «VOL»2. II.；«CONT»3ENTS« OF»1« V»3«OL»2. II.；«I»2«.»2；«1»6« Table»6« of»5« Contents»4
patterns.context: 目录、章节编号、罗马数字及标题排版附近出现激活；强度落在不同片段，不能确认是格式本身触发。

patterns.name: 金融词汇邻接
patterns.context: 贷款、利率、还款等金融词汇附近有一组激活，但文本严重破碎，无法确定触发条件是否为金融语义。

patterns.name: 明显无关的异常拼接
patterns.trigger: «rel»5«inger»2« Archives»5 download The National Basketball« still»7；«episode»7« audi»4«ob»3«ook»5
patterns.context: 语义跳跃、词语拼接或类似机器生成/抓取噪声的文本中，多个不相干片段激活。

en.description: Activations occur on within-word subword fragments, an, title catalogs and numbered formatting, Q&A markers, and several ordinary words; there are also each and a few anomalous word forms, spellings, and scattered web activations, with no unified semantic condition.

patterns.name: Within-word segmentation and subword boundaries
patterns.context: Activations often fall on fragments of words split into multiple tokens, especially subsequent within-word fragments; the specific fragments and positions are inconsistent.
patterns.domain: Cross-domain text, ordinary text, and novel formatting

patterns.name: Word-initial an
patterns.context: In phrases followed by words beginning with vowels, such as “an ultrasound,” “an eSpe...,” and “an operational”; nearby tokens such as «a» also activate more weakly.
patterns.domain: Medical abstracts, emails, and general English

patterns.name: Numbering, catalogs, and uppercase title formatting
patterns.context: In titles, catalogs, or prominent all-caps formatting, numbers, Roman numerals, abbreviations, or words are split into fragments; line breaks may also occur nearby.

patterns.name: English word endings and within-word fragments
patterns.context: Scattered activations occur on within-word fragments and whole words in ordinary words or proper nouns, with no consistent semantic or syntactic condition.

patterns.name: Anomalous word forms or possibly garbled text
patterns.context: A longer NIH project description contains consecutive within-word fragments, some of which look like misaligned or anomalous word forms when concatenated; web fragments also contain word-fragment activations.
patterns.domain: NIH project texts and web text

patterns.name: Q&A markers and slashes
patterns.context: The Q: at the beginning of a question and compounds separated by slashes show prominent activations on punctuation or separators themselves.

patterns.name: Each and quantity expressions
patterns.context: Activations occur on each (and nearby words such as are and dedicated); the two instances appear respectively in educational promotional copy and mixed text.
patterns.domain: Educational promotional copy and general text

patterns.name: Likely proper nouns or irregular spellings
patterns.context: Phrases contain unusual capitalization or spelling, or a sequence of common short words; there is insufficient evidence to determine a shared semantic pattern.
patterns.domain: Puzzle emails and NIH project texts

patterns.name: Scattered activations not explained by a clear pattern
patterns.context: Activations are scattered across ordinary words in multi-topic, semantically discontinuous web passages, with no reliable shared trigger condition.

patterns.name: Quantity/age words in an incomplete phrase
patterns.context: Describes rare and elderly populations; activations fall on the adjective, hyphen, and aged. This is a single instance and does not confirm a stable semantic pattern.

9_2056.concept: 词片段与文本格式线索
9_2056.description: 激活分布在词内子词片段、an、标题目录与编号排版、问答标记及若干普通词上；另有 each 和少数异常词形、拼写及散乱网页激活，未见统一语义条件。

patterns.name: 词内分片与子词边界
patterns.context: 激活常落在词被拆分成多个 token 的片段上，尤其是词中后续片段；但具体片段和位置并不一致。
patterns.domain: 跨领域文本、普通文本及小说排版

patterns.name: 词首的 an
patterns.context: 在后接元音开头词的短语中，如“an ultrasound”“an eSpe...”“an operational”；另有«a»等邻近 token 激活较弱。
patterns.domain: 医学摘要、邮件及一般英语

patterns.name: 编号、目录与大写标题排版
patterns.context: 标题、目录或醒目的全大写排版中，编号、罗马数字、缩写或词语被拆成片段；附近也可能出现换行。

patterns.name: 英语词尾与词中片段
patterns.context: 零散地激活于普通词或专名的词内片段及完整词，未见一致的词义或句法条件。

patterns.name: 异常词形或疑似乱码文本
patterns.context: 较长的 NIH 项目描述中出现连续的词内分片，部分片段拼接后像是错位或异常词形；网页片段也有词片段激活。
patterns.domain: NIH 项目文本及网页文本

patterns.name: 问答标记与斜线
patterns.context: 问题文本开头的 Q:，以及斜线分隔的复合词中，标点或分隔符本身激活突出。

patterns.name: 各自与数量表达
patterns.context: 出现 each（及附近的 are、dedicated 等词）时有激活；两处用法分别处于教育宣传语和混杂文本中。
patterns.domain: 教育宣传语及一般文本

patterns.name: 疑似专名或不规则拼写
patterns.context: 短语中含有不寻常的大小写或拼写形式，或出现一串常见短词；没有足够证据判断其共同语义。
patterns.domain: 谜题邮件及 NIH 项目文本

patterns.name: 无法由明确模式解释的散乱激活
patterns.context: 多主题、语义跳跃的网页片段中散布于普通词上的激活，未呈现可靠的共同触发条件。

patterns.name: 残缺短语中的数量/年龄词
patterns.context: 描述罕见且高龄的人群，激活落在形容词、连字符和 aged 上；单例，不能确认是稳定语义模式。

en.description: Activation is primarily associated with an and several internal word fragments, especially in segmented proper nouns, words, and research text; scattered triggers also include all, years, drug names, and chemical names, without forming a stable semantic pattern.

patterns.name: Word-internal suffix “ing”
patterns.context: High activation falls on a later subword fragment within a segmented word or adjective; one example is not ing, possibly indicating a broader pattern of internal word fragments.

patterns.name: Tokenization of the indefinite article an
patterns.context: Activation concentrates on the indefinite article an, followed by different words such as ultrasound, exceptionally, operational, and objective.
patterns.domain: Medical abstracts, research text, and email

patterns.name: Internal subwords in proper nouns or words
patterns.context: Words are split into multiple tokens, with activation biased toward internal fragments; examples include experience, eSpeak, and Quatro, but their meanings differ.

patterns.name: Suffix or internal fragment “eth/et”
patterns.context: Internal word segmentation occurs, but not all similar fragments activate strongly; it is unclear whether a specific suffix is the trigger.

patterns.name: all in a quotation
patterns.context: Appears at the beginning of a quoted sentence, followed by “of the various demonstrations”; this is a single example, with no confirmable condition.

patterns.name: Initial repetition of the proper noun Quatro
patterns.context: The same word appears repeatedly at the beginning of an entry, with the segmented parts Qu/atro activating; this may relate to internal word fragments such as eSpeak in other materials.

patterns.name: Various scattered subword activations
patterns.context: Ordinary words and years in historical text, internal fragments of drug names, and initial fragments of chemical structure names activate separately, with no shared semantics or stable contextual condition apparent.
patterns.domain: Historical art history, medicine, chemical abstracts

patterns.name: Structural markers and section-initial elements
patterns.context: Medical paper subsection headings, separator lines, and elements at the beginning of following sections; headings and markers themselves activate weakly, with strong activation mainly on an.

9_2056.description: 激活以 an 及若干词内子词片段为主，尤其出现在拆分的专名、词语和科研文本中；另有 all、年份、药物与化学名称等零散触发，未形成稳定语义模式。

patterns.name: 词内后缀“ing”
patterns.context: 高激活落在分词或形容词内部的后续子词片段；一个例子并非 ing，可能只是更广泛的词内片段模式。
patterns.domain: 科研摘要及研究资助文本

patterns.name: 不定冠词 an 的分词
patterns.context: 激活集中在不定冠词 an；其后接 ultrasound、exceptionally、operational、objective 等不同词。
patterns.domain: 医学摘要、科研文本及邮件

patterns.name: 专名或词语的内部子词
patterns.context: 词语被拆成多个 token，激活偏向内部片段；包含 experience、eSpeak 和 Quatro，但具体词义各异。

patterns.name: 后缀或词内片段“eth/et”
patterns.context: 出现词内拆分，但并非所有同类片段都强激活；是否由特定后缀触发不明确。
patterns.domain: 医学文本、历史艺术文本

patterns.name: 引语中的 all
patterns.context: 位于引号中的句子开头，后接“of the various demonstrations”；仅此一例，缺少可确认条件。

patterns.name: 专名 Quatro 的词首复现
patterns.context: 同一词在条目开头重复出现，拆分部分 Qu/atro 激活；与其他材料中的 eSpeak 等词内片段可能相关。

patterns.name: 多种零散子词激活
patterns.context: 历史文本中的普通词和年份、药物名称的词内片段、化学结构名称的词首片段分别激活，未见共同语义或稳定上下文条件。
patterns.domain: 历史艺术史、医学、化学摘要

patterns.name: 结构标记与段首成分
patterns.context: 医学论文小节标题、分隔线及其后段首成分；标题和标记本身激活较弱，强激活主要出现在 an。

en.description: Strong activations are distributed across the subwords in washout and hyperpolarization, repeated name fragments in EuroParl, numeric table formats, and several ordinary English words or pronouns. Aside from triggers within some subwords, no consistent semantic or contextual pattern is evident.

patterns.name: wash in “washout”
patterns.context: Appears in the biological abstract term “washout resistance”; activation is concentrated in the beginning of washout.

patterns.name: polar in a hyperpolarization term
patterns.context: Appears in a technical term describing activity-dependent chronic hyperpolarization.

patterns.name: Subwords in names
patterns.context: These subwords appear in consecutive repeated name fragments; the same string is repeated in two paragraphs, and another similar string also triggers activation.
patterns.domain: Names or proper nouns in EuroParl text

patterns.name: Format markers in numeric tables
patterns.context: Several decimal-like values recur in a sequence of numbered data; activation is scattered, with no clear trigger tied to a single number.

patterns.name: Sporadic triggers in general English text
patterns.context: Appear respectively in “never goes offline,” a narrative context with the pronoun he, and the subword fragment “androgynous”; no identifiable shared contextual condition links them.

9_2194.description: 强激活分散于 washout、hyperpolarization 的词片、EuroParl 中重复姓名片段、数值表格格式，以及若干普通英语词语或代词；除部分词片内部触发外，未见统一语义或上下文模式。

patterns.name: “washout”中的 wash
patterns.context: 出现在生物学摘要的术语 “washout resistance” 中；激活集中于 washout 的开头部分。

patterns.name: 超极化术语中的 polar
patterns.context: 出现在描述神经活动依赖性慢性超极化的专业术语中。

patterns.name: 人名中的词片
patterns.context: 这些词片出现在连续重复的人名/姓名片段中；同一串在两个段落重复，另一个相似串也触发。
patterns.domain: EuroParl 文本中的姓名或专名

patterns.name: 数字表格中的格式符
patterns.context: 一行按序号列出的数值数据中，多个类似小数的数值反复出现；激活较分散，未见明显单一数字触发。

patterns.name: 一般英语文本中的零散触发
patterns.context: 分别出现在 “never goes offline”、代词 he 的叙述语境，以及单词片段 “androgynous” 中；彼此缺少可确认的共同上下文条件。

en.description: Activations are scattered across the English pronoun he, subword fragments of several long words or names, decimal-number sequences, and the title word Love. They vary substantially across corpora and contexts, making it difficult to identify a single stable trigger.

patterns.name: washout morpheme boundary
patterns.context: In a medical question, “washout” appears, with activations concentrated at the wash/out subword split.

patterns.name: English pronoun he
patterns.context: In English narration or conversation, he is the subject, followed by a modal or linking verb or another predicate; activation falls mainly on he.

patterns.name: Within-word fragments in a title
patterns.context: In the title “androgynous man essay,” androgynous is split into several subword fragments, with stronger activation on later fragments.

patterns.name: Subword fragments of names or foreign words
patterns.context: In EuroParl text, names or foreign/compound words are split by the tokenizer; similar beginnings and within-word fragments recur.

patterns.name: Number sequences and decimal tables
patterns.context: Multiline numerical sequences after a line break, consisting of numbers, colons, and decimal points.

patterns.name: Within-word fragments of technical terms
patterns.context: In neuroscience paper abstracts, long technical terms are split, with activation on an internal fragment of hyperpolarization.

patterns.name: Love in titles/text
patterns.context: Repeated Love appears in title- or lyric-style text, but activation does not consistently fall on the word.

9_2194.description: 激活分散在英语 he 代词、若干长词或名字的子词片段、数字小数序列及 Love 标题词上；不同语料和语境差异明显，难以归为单一稳定触发条件。

patterns.name: washout 词缀边界
patterns.context: 医学题目中出现“washout”，激活集中在 wash/out 的子词拆分处。

patterns.name: 英语代词 he
patterns.context: 英语叙述或口语中，he 作主语，后接情态/系动词或其他谓语；激活主要落在 he。

patterns.name: 标题中的词内片段
patterns.context: 标题“androgynous man essay”中，单词 androgynous 被拆成多个子词片段，后段激活较强。

patterns.name: 名字或外语词的子词片段
patterns.context: EuroParl 文本中的人名或外语/复合词被分词器拆分；相似开头与词内片段重复出现。

patterns.name: 数字序列与小数表格
patterns.context: 换行后以编号和冒号、小数点组成的多行数值序列。

patterns.name: 专业术语的词内片段
patterns.context: 神经科学论文摘要中，长专业术语被拆分，激活落在 hyperpolarization 的内部片段。

patterns.name: 标题/文本中的 Love
patterns.context: 标题或歌词样式文本中出现重复的 Love；但激活并不稳定地落在该词上。

en.description: Activations are scattered across heterogeneous text: proper names and within-word substrings, the pronoun he, number sequences, email headers, and book-review titles. The fragment -polar, he, and several proper-name fragments recur in different contexts, but no unified semantic or formatting pattern is apparent.

patterns.name: Proper-name fragments in personal names
patterns.context: Names or proper nouns are split into multiple subword tokens; one occurs in a book-review byline, another in title-style text.

patterns.name: Word-final fragment -polar
patterns.context: Occurs in scientific terms, either following “hyper” in “hyperpolarization” or in expressions such as “non-polar” and “polar surface”; activation may also respond to the fragment itself within a word.
patterns.domain: Neuroscience, biomedicine, and peptide chemistry abstracts

patterns.name: Sequence and decimal-number format
patterns.context: Multiple space-separated number–decimal sequences, with 0 after a colon followed by decimals; activation spans digits, punctuation, and parts of digit strings.

patterns.name: he in everyday conversation
patterns.context: The pronoun he occurs in informal narration, especially in “he's pretty cute” and “he might… when he’ll…”; nearby words also show weaker activation.

patterns.name: Within-word fragment in washout
patterns.context: “washout” occurs in the expression “washout resistance,” referring to a material or pharmacological property.

patterns.name: Fragment of a compound medical term
patterns.context: In “arteriovenous malformation,” activation is concentrated on the later part of the within-word fragment “ovenous”; nearby medical words include “headache” and “treatment.”
patterns.domain: Medical case reports or clinical literature abstracts

patterns.name: Date fields in email headers
patterns.context: From and Date fields in an email header, including an address, weekday, date, year, and time.

patterns.name: Love in a book title or phrase
patterns.context: After “Review:” appears the title “Love 3.0: Love never goes offline”; activation is especially concentrated on the second Love and never.
patterns.domain: Web book reviews or promotional copy

9_2194.description: 激活分散于异质文本：专名与词内子串、he 代词、数字序列、邮件头及书评标题；其中 -polar、he 和若干专名片段在不同上下文中重复，未见统一语义或格式模式。

patterns.name: 人名中的专名片段
patterns.context: 姓名或专名被拆成多个子词 token；前者出现在书评署名，后者出现在标题式文本。

patterns.name: 词尾片段 -polar
patterns.context: 出现在科学术语中，前接“hyper”构成“hyperpolarization”，或出现在“non-polar”“polar surface”等表达中；也可能对词内该片段本身敏感。
patterns.domain: 神经科学、生物医学、肽化学摘要

patterns.name: 序列与小数数值格式
patterns.context: 多组以空格分隔的编号—小数值序列，冒号后为 0，随后是小数；激活覆盖数字、标点和部分数字串。

patterns.name: 日常口语中的 he
patterns.context: 代词 he 出现在非正式叙述中，尤其是“he's pretty cute”和“he might… when he’ll…”；附近词也有较弱激活。

patterns.name: washout 词内片段
patterns.context: “washout”出现在“washout resistance”这一材料或药理性质表述中。

patterns.name: 复合医学术语片段
patterns.context: “arteriovenous malformation”中，激活集中在词内“ovenous”后段；附近还有“headache”“treatment”等医学词。
patterns.domain: 医学病例或临床文献摘要

patterns.name: 邮件头日期字段
patterns.context: 邮件头中的 From 与 Date 字段，包含地址、星期、日期、年份及时间。

patterns.name: 书名或短语中的 Love
patterns.context: “Review:”之后出现标题“Love 3.0: Love never goes offline”，激活特别集中于第二个 Love 和 never。

en.description: Activations are distributed across hyperpolarization terminology, washout, fragments within long words or proper nouns, expressions of an ongoing state with never, and email salutation/signature formats; trigger points and contexts vary considerably.

patterns.name: hyperpolarization terminology
patterns.context: In neuroscience or physiology titles describing hyperpolarization and related factors; activation falls on multiple subword fragments within the term.

patterns.name: washout in a technical term
patterns.context: In a biology paper title, washout appears with resistance to describe resistance to the washout of an effect.

patterns.name: Fragments within proper nouns or word forms
patterns.context: Activation is distributed across subword fragments within longer words or proper nouns; examples involve a title word, a place name, a tumor type, and a vascular malformation, with no shared semantic condition.
patterns.domain: Web text, encyclopedias, and PubMed abstracts

patterns.name: never and ongoing states
patterns.context: The sentence says an entity has continually maintained a state or activity: a music service “never goes offline,” or a church “never ceased operating.”

patterns.name: Email line breaks and salutations
patterns.context: Email salutations and line breaks, or names, titles, and line breaks in signatures; activation falls mainly on formatting markers and name/title fragments.

9_2194.description: 激活分散于超极化术语、washout、长词或专名内部片段、never 持续状态表达，以及邮件称呼/签名格式；各例触发点与语境差异较大。

patterns.name: hyperpolarization terminology
patterns.context: 神经科学或生理学标题中，描述超极化及相关因子；激活落在术语内部多个子词片段上。
patterns.domain: PubMed 摘要，神经科学/生理学

patterns.name: 专业词中的 washout
patterns.context: 生物学论文标题中，washout 与 resistance 连用，描述某种效应的洗脱抵抗性。

patterns.name: 专名或词形内部的片段
patterns.context: 激活分布在较长词或专名内部的子词片段；这些例子分别涉及标题中的词、地名、肿瘤类型和血管畸形，未见共同语义条件。
patterns.domain: 网页文本、百科和 PubMed 摘要

patterns.name: never 与持续状态
patterns.context: 句中说明某对象一直未停止某种状态或活动：歌曲服务“never goes offline”，教堂“never ceased operating”。

patterns.name: 邮件换行与称呼
patterns.context: 邮件正文的称呼和换行，或签名中的姓名、职务及换行；激活主要落在格式标记和姓名/职位片段。

en.description: Activations are most concentrated in medical titles or abstracts, but are distributed across subwords within technical terms, common words, punctuation, and numbers. Email greetings/signatures, pronouns and modals in narration, and an isolated book-review title also appear; no single stable trigger is evident.

patterns.name: Subwords across word boundaries in medical titles
patterns.context: Activations fall within medical terms split into multiple tokens, especially technical terms or the beginning of a title; they cannot be unified by a particular affix or term.

patterns.name: Strong subword splits within words
patterns.context: Activations occur within words split into multiple tokens, across different word classes and positions; some examples involve medical vocabulary, others proper names.

patterns.name: Common words and punctuation in medical titles
patterns.context: In title-style medical text, activation extends to common words, conjunctions, punctuation, and numbers, rather than being limited to technical terms or token boundaries.

patterns.name: Email greetings, signatures, and line breaks
patterns.context: Activations occur in an opening greeting or short phrase in an email, or in a signature block consisting of a name and title; line breaks also show strong activation.

patterns.name: Pronouns and modal words in narrative sentences
patterns.context: In ordinary narrative sentences, activations concentrate on sentence-initial conjunctions, pronouns, and phrases expressing possibility or thought.

patterns.name: Words in a particular book title or heading
patterns.context: In a book-review title and author byline, activation occurs on title words, numbers, and split parts of the author's surname; there is no support from other matching contexts.

9_2194.description: 激活最集中于医学标题或摘要，但分布在术语内部的子词、普通词、标点和数字；另见邮件称呼/签名、叙事中的代词情态词及孤立书评标题，未显出单一稳定触发特征。

patterns.name: 医学标题中的跨词边界子词
patterns.context: 激活落在被拆分成多个 token 的医学词语内部，尤其是术语或标题开头；但不能统一为某个特定词缀或术语。
patterns.domain: PubMed 医学论文标题/摘要

patterns.name: 单词内部的强子词分段
patterns.context: 激活出现在一个词被拆成多个 token 的内部，不同词类和位置均有出现；部分例子与医学词汇有关，另有专名。

patterns.name: 医学标题中的常见词及标点
patterns.trigger: «:»7« a»7« study»5« of»6« 250»6；« growth»10« and»8« mass»7« are»7« preserved»8；« surgery»10«,»6« safety»8« and»7
patterns.context: 标题式医学文本中，激活扩展到普通词、连接词、标点及数字，并非只集中在专业术语或分词边界。
patterns.domain: PubMed 医学论文标题/摘要

patterns.name: 邮件称呼、签名及换行
patterns.context: 激活出现在邮件开头的称呼/短句，或姓名与职务构成的签名块；换行也有较强激活。

patterns.name: 叙事句中的代词与情态词
patterns.trigger: «And»7« he»9« might»7« start»6« to»6« wonder»8« when»7« he»9«’»5«ll»6
patterns.context: 普通叙事句中，激活集中在句首连接词、代词及表达可能性或思考的词组。

patterns.name: 特定书名或标题中的词语
patterns.trigger: «Review»5«:»6« Love»6« 3»5«.»6«0»7«:»6« Love»6« never»10« goes»6« offline»7« by»6« Pat»6« T»6«res»7«na»6«↵»5
patterns.context: 一段书评标题及作者署名中，标题词语、数字和作者姓氏的拆分部分均有激活；缺乏其他相同上下文支持。

en.description: Activations cover varied formats: music encyclopedia entries, transitions between definitions and theorems in mathematics papers, project and medical abstracts, garbled legal text, payment error-handling code, and email headers. The patterns differ considerably, with no reliable shared meaning or semantic trigger.

patterns.name: Release descriptions in song/album entries
patterns.context: A music entry begins with a title or work name, followed by information about the singer/band, work type, and release; activation often falls on common narrative words and “label.”

patterns.name: Transitions between definitions and theorems in mathematics papers
patterns.context: Transition language in a mathematics paper, after formal objects, sets, or thresholds, leading into a definition or a review of a theorem.

patterns.name: Project proposals and descriptions of research subjects
patterns.context: A project proposal lists research topics and describes experimental factors or research subjects.

patterns.name: Medical title-like phrases
patterns.context: A paper-title fragment consisting of a disease/tumor category followed by a colon and a research description.

patterns.name: Unusual characters or garbled text
patterns.context: The text consists mainly of illegible symbols and letter fragments, with no stable, readable semantic structure.

patterns.name: Error handling and error-code checks
patterns.context: Catches a payment connection exception, reads the exception data, and checks whether it contains a specified error code.

patterns.name: Raw email message headers
patterns.context: Email header fields in forwarded or quoted content, followed by the sender and send time.

9_2194.description: 激活覆盖多种格式：音乐百科作品介绍、数学论文的定义/定理衔接、项目与医学摘要、乱码法律文本、支付异常代码及邮件头。可见模式彼此差异较大，尚无可靠共同词义或语义触发点。

patterns.name: 歌曲/专辑条目中的发行描述
patterns.trigger: “is a debut single by”“song … was released as a single”“studio album … was released on”“sub-label”
patterns.context: 音乐作品条目以标题或作品名开头，随后介绍歌手/乐队、作品类型及发行信息；激活常落在常见叙述词及“label”等词上。

patterns.name: 数学论文中的定义与定理衔接
patterns.context: 数学论文在形式化对象、集合或阈值后，转入定义或回顾定理的段落衔接语。

patterns.name: 项目提案与研究对象描述
patterns.trigger: “Proposed projects include:”以及“effect of ions … potassium and calcium”
patterns.context: 项目提案列举研究内容，并说明实验因素或研究对象。

patterns.name: 医学题名式短语
patterns.context: 以疾病/肿瘤类别加冒号及研究说明构成的论文题名片段。

patterns.name: 异常字符或乱码文本
patterns.context: 文本主要由难以辨认的符号、字母片段组成，缺少可读的稳定语义结构。

patterns.name: 异常处理与错误码检查
patterns.context: 捕获支付连接异常，读取异常数据并检查其中是否含指定错误码。

patterns.name: 邮件原始消息头
patterns.context: 邮件转发或引用内容中的邮件头字段，后接发件人及发送时间。

en.description: The strongest activation usually falls on few in a few. Other sporadic triggers include the relative pronoun who, Then at the start of mathematical derivations or narrative sentences, the proper-name fragment Bel, and the stock abbreviation TX; these span domains with no single stable meaning.

patterns.name: few / a few phrases
patterns.context: The quantifier a few modifies a count noun; the strongest activation falls on few
patterns.domain: Spoken language, forum discussions, and general narrative

patterns.name: who in relative clauses
patterns.context: who introduces a relative clause modifying person
patterns.domain: Patent background sections, formal explanatory prose

patterns.name: Then introducing a derivation step
patterns.context: In a mathematical derivation, introduces subsequent conditions and definitions after a formula or assumption

patterns.name: Bel fragment in the proper noun Belgrave
patterns.context: A word begins with Bel; the same passage also contains proper-name fragments such as Belgrave and Beltrami

patterns.name: Then in theological quotations
patterns.context: In a biblical parable quotation, Then appears at the beginning of a narrative sentence

patterns.name: TX company abbreviation fragment
patterns.context: TX appears within a company abbreviation in a stock example

patterns.name: Other unexplained sporadic activations
patterns.context: Local word fragments or tokenization boundaries vary; the available context is insufficient to identify a stable condition

9_2194.description: 最强处多落在 a few 的 few；另有关系代词 who、数学推导或叙事句首的 Then、Bel 专名片段及股票缩写 TX 等零散触发，跨领域且无单一稳定语义。

patterns.name: few／a few 的短语
patterns.trigger: “a few pulls”“a few months”“a few years”“a few programming languages”中的 «few»9/10
patterns.context: 出现量词 a few，修饰可数名词；激活最强处落在 few
patterns.domain: 口语、论坛讨论及一般叙述

patterns.name: 关系从句中的 who
patterns.context: who 引导修饰 person 的关系从句
patterns.domain: 专利背景技术、正式说明文

patterns.name: Then 引出推导步骤
patterns.context: 数学推导中，在公式或假设之后引出后续条件与定义

patterns.name: Belgrave 专名片段
patterns.context: 单词以 Bel 开头；同段还出现 Belgrave、Beltrami 等专名片段
patterns.domain: 百科条目、专利医学文本

patterns.name: 神学引文中的 Then
patterns.context: 圣经寓言引文中，Then 位于叙事句首
patterns.domain: 维基百科宗教条目、圣经引文

patterns.name: TX 公司缩写片段
patterns.context: 股票举例中，公司名缩写内部出现 TX

patterns.name: unexplained 其余零散激活
patterns.trigger: 未发现可由上述模式解释的明确共同触发项；如 “«happ»”“«cra»”“«re»generative”
patterns.context: 局部词片段或分词边界各异，现有上下文不足以确定稳定条件

en.concept: English syntactic introducers and title words
en.description: Activations often fall on linking or introducing elements such as that, when, what, and Will; a medical proper-name fragment, Spindle, also appears once. A few passages have title or explanatory prose structures, while the passage about an Irish band has no clear corresponding clue.

patterns.name: that as a sentence connector
patterns.context: that is followed by a clause, temporal/relative clause, or statement; it recurs within the passage

patterns.name: Will in an interrogative title
patterns.context: In a title-like question, Will appears after the subject or noun phrase and expresses the future or a need

patterns.name: that in relative clauses
patterns.context: that introduces a relative clause describing a noun, as in “centers that offers” and “issues that can prevent”

patterns.name: what as a condition or topic introducer
patterns.context: what at the beginning of a sentence or clause introduces the matter being asked about or discussed

patterns.name: when in temporal/conditional clauses
patterns.context: Introduces a temporal or situational clause, followed by a description of what happens in that circumstance

patterns.name: Repeated fragment of a technical name
patterns.context: A tumor name recurs in a medical title; strong activation falls on its segmented subword fragments

patterns.name: that as a determiner
patterns.context: that occurs in demonstrative constructions referring to previously mentioned content, as in “that period” or “that …”

9_2194.concept: 英语句法引导词与标题词
9_2194.description: 激活多落在 that、when、what、Will 等连接或引导成分上，也出现一次医学专名片段 Spindle；少数段落呈标题或说明文结构，爱尔兰乐队段无明显对应线索。

patterns.name: 句中连接词 that
patterns.context: that 后接从句、时间/关系从句或陈述内容；在段落中反复出现

patterns.name: 疑问标题中的 Will
patterns.context: 标题式疑问句中，Will 位于主语或名词短语之后，表示未来/需求

patterns.name: 关系从句 that
patterns.context: that 引导描述名词的关系从句，如“centers that offers”“issues that can prevent”
patterns.domain: 百科说明、产品/实用说明

patterns.name: 条件或话题引入词 what
patterns.context: 句首或从句开头的 what 引出所询问、讨论的内容

patterns.name: 时间/条件从句 when
patterns.context: 引出时间或情境从句，后续说明某时发生的状况

patterns.name: 重复的专业名称片段
patterns.context: 医学标题中重复出现的肿瘤名称；高激活落在被拆分词片段上

patterns.name: 限定词 that
patterns.context: that 位于指示性结构中，指向此前提到的内容，如“that period”“that …”

en.description: All ten passages show strong activation (usually 9 or 10) on the relative word «which», in both relative clauses and supplementary clauses. In a few contexts, pronouns or predicates within the clause also activate more weakly.

patterns.name: which in relative clauses
patterns.context: Appears at the start of a relative or supplementary clause within a sentence, followed by an auxiliary, pronoun, or predicate; activation is not limited to a particular meaning or grammatical domain.

patterns.name: Full relative-clause structure
patterns.context: Relative clauses often add information after a preceding noun or proposition; as in the previous pattern, but activation may also be sensitive to the subsequent relative-clause structure.
patterns.domain: Books, academic writing, encyclopedias, forums, emails, and legal text

patterns.name: Subjects or referring expressions within which-clauses
patterns.context: Referring words or predicates within relative clauses sometimes also receive positive activation; for example, «which they are able to give» and «which were included».

9_2194.description: 十段均在关系词«which»处出现强激活（多为9或10），涵盖关系从句与补充说明用法；少数上下文中从句内的代词或谓语也有较弱激活。

patterns.name: 关系从句中的 which
patterns.context: 出现于句中关系从句或补充说明从句的引导位置，后接助动词、代词或谓语；激活不局限于特定意义或语法领域。

patterns.name: 完整关系从句结构
patterns.trigger: «which»后接从句内容，如«which will show»、«which can be found»、«which is really beautiful»
patterns.context: 相对从句常在前文名词或命题之后补充说明；与前一模式相同，但可能还对后续关系从句结构敏感。
patterns.domain: 书籍、学术、百科、论坛、邮件及法律文本

patterns.name: which从句中的主语或指代形式
patterns.context: 关系从句中的指代词或谓语有时也获正激活；例如«which they are able to give»、«which were included»。

en.description: The most stable trigger is who in relative clauses; if, When, and interrogative or subordinate introducers such as where/how also activate strongly. Several scattered pronouns, sentence-initial It, and ordinary it also activate, but cannot be explained by a single pattern.

patterns.name: Relative pronoun who introducing information about people
patterns.context: who follows a noun referring to a person or group and introduces a relative clause describing their identity, experience, attributes, or actions; activation is concentrated on who itself.
patterns.domain: Multiple genres: biographies, historical argument, religious texts, encyclopedia entries, and general dialogue

patterns.name: if introducing a condition or hypothesis
patterns.context: if introduces a conditional or hypothetical clause; examples concern whether there is truth and a hypothetical dishonest answer to avoid embarrassment.

patterns.name: When as a temporal introducer
patterns.context: When introduces a historical situation or temporal clause, followed by a description of an event or circumstance.

patterns.name: where as an interrogative word
patterns.context: In a series of fundamental questions about life or the world, where asks about origin.

patterns.name: how as an interrogative word
patterns.context: At the beginning of a question giving an example or asking about the cause of an event, asks how it happened.

patterns.name: What as an interrogative word
patterns.context: In dialogue, What introduces a hypothetical follow-up question; activation is weaker here.

patterns.name: Sentence-initial It in information structure
patterns.context: Sentence-initial It picks up the previous context and begins a statement about a preceding result or situation, rather than a salient question or relative clause.

patterns.name: Lexical or tokenized it
patterns.context: Used as a pronoun or dummy subject in ordinary sentences, appearing in a judgment about chance and a description of a natural process; unlike the high-activation interrogative-word pattern.

patterns.name: Other context-dependent pronoun triggers
patterns.context: Pronouns occur in different syntactic positions: he as the subject of a report, ones referring to care programs, you as the addressee of a question, and we in a parallel question about identity/origin; they do not form a unified syntactic pattern.
patterns.domain: News, online dialogue, religious texts, and encyclopedia text

9_2194.description: 最稳定的触发是关系从句中的 who，另对 if、When 及 where/how 等疑问或从属引导词有较强激活；另有若干分散的代词、句首 It 与普通 it 激活，不能统一解释。

patterns.name: 关系代词 who 引出人物说明
patterns.context: who 位于人物或群体名词之后，引出其身份、经历、属性或行动的关系从句；激活集中在 who 本身。
patterns.domain: 多种文体：人物传记、历史议论、宗教文本、百科条目及一般对话

patterns.name: 条件或假设引导词 if
patterns.context: if 引出条件或假设从句；分别涉及是否有真相，以及为避免尴尬而作不诚实回答的假设。

patterns.name: 时间引导词 When
patterns.context: When 引出历史情境或时间从句，后接事件或情境描述。
patterns.domain: 引述、历史或公共议题论述

patterns.name: 疑问词 where
patterns.context: 在提出人生或世界根本问题的并列疑问中，用 where 询问来源。

patterns.name: 疑问词 how
patterns.context: 在举例或追问事件缘由的疑问句开头，询问事情如何发生。

patterns.name: 疑问词 What
patterns.context: 在对话中以 What 引出假设性追问；该处激活较弱。

patterns.name: 信息结构中的句首 It
patterns.context: 句首 It 承接前文，开启对前述结果或情况的陈述，而非显著的疑问或关系从句。

patterns.name: 特定词汇／分词 it
patterns.context: 在普通句中作代词或形式主语，分别出现在 chance 判断及自然过程的叙述中；与高激活的疑问词模式不同。

patterns.name: 语境性强的其他代词触发
patterns.context: 代词处于不同句法位置：he 作报道中的主语，ones 指代照护项目，you 作提问对象，we 出现在身份／来源的并列问题中；无法归为统一句法模式。
patterns.domain: 新闻、网络对话、宗教及百科文本

en.concept: Generic reference and expressions of possibility, with additional domain-word triggers
en.description: Activations are scattered: common patterns include generic entities or scope (anyone, anything, any), possibility and inferential questions. Other local patterns include quantum algorithms, reviews of books for boys, fragmented Spanish subwords, and negation.

patterns.name: Generic entities and ranges
patterns.context: In statements about privacy, cost, ability, behavior, or possibility, words referring generically to people, things, or scope activate, often in expressions like anything/anyone.

patterns.name: Questions and possibility inferences
patterns.context: When raising or discussing possibilities, inferences, or imaginings, activations appear near interrogative words, modal verbs, or generic objects.

patterns.name: Quantum algorithm topic words
patterns.context: When introducing research progress, papers, or reviews on quantum algorithms, activation is strongest on algorithms at the end of the topic phrase.

patterns.name: Spanish tokenization and negation
patterns.context: In continuous Spanish text, multiple words are split into subword tokens; the negation word no has the strongest activation in the sentence.

patterns.name: Suitability of a book for boys
patterns.context: Evaluates whether a book is suitable for boys to read; nearby text discusses literary quality, interest, or publication.

patterns.name: Word-initial fragments and proper nouns
patterns.context: Activation is distributed across fragmented Spanish subwords and several common short fragments in sentences, with no stable semantic condition corresponding to the other passages.

9_2194.concept: 泛指与可能性表达，兼有领域词触发
9_2194.description: 激活较分散：常见于泛指对象或范围（anyone、anything、any）、可能性与疑问推断；另有量子算法、男孩读物评价、西班牙语碎片化子词及否定词等局部模式。

patterns.name: 泛指对象与数量范围
patterns.context: 在关于隐私、费用、能力、行为或可能性的陈述中，泛指人、事物或范围的词受到激活，常出现在 anything/anyone 一类表达里。

patterns.name: 疑问结构与可能性推断
patterns.context: 提出或讨论可能性、推断、想象时，疑问词、情态动词或泛指宾语附近出现激活。

patterns.name: 量子算法主题词
patterns.context: 介绍量子算法研究进展、论文或综述时，主题短语末尾的 algorithms 激活最强。

patterns.name: 西班牙语分词与否定词
patterns.context: 西班牙语连续文本中，多个词被切分成子词标记；句中否定词 no 激活最强。

patterns.name: 书籍对男孩的适读评价
patterns.context: 评价书籍适合男孩阅读，周围谈及文学质量、趣味或出版情况。

patterns.name: 词首残片与专名
patterns.context: 激活分布在西班牙语词语的碎片化子词以及句中若干常见短片段，未见与其他段落稳定对应的语义条件。

en.description: Activations concentrate on words referring to things, objects, or categories, especially things, something, anything, and plural entity nouns. Contexts span encyclopedias, forums, law, technology, history, and mathematical discussion, with no restriction to a single domain.

patterns.name: Generic things and categories of things
patterns.context: In questions, evaluations, or explanations, refers generically to a thing, imaginable object, or category of things; strong activation often falls on words such as things/something/anything.

patterns.name: Plural nouns referring to entities or objects
patterns.context: Concrete plural nouns refer to countable items, entities, or objects; no fixed domain is required.
patterns.domain: Encyclopedias, history, law, and technical discussions

patterns.name: Products qualified by value or quantity
patterns.context: Discusses whether certain valuable things would still be produced under particular conditions.

patterns.name: Technical objects and their versions or modules
patterns.context: Refers to a particular version of a software module and describes the release or review of related proof.

patterns.name: Semantic referent
patterns.context: When explaining a word's meaning, uses something that to introduce the object or property being described.

patterns.name: Objects or types in formulas
patterns.context: In discussions of mathematical formulas and their relationships, refers generically to objects occurring or appearing in them.

9_2194.description: 激活集中在指称事物、对象或类别的词，尤其是 things、something、anything 及复数实体名词；具体语境横跨百科、论坛、法律、技术、历史与数学讨论，未显示单一领域限制。

patterns.name: 泛指事物与事物类别
patterns.context: 在疑问、评价或解释语境中，泛指某种事物、可想象对象或事物类别；强度常落在 things/something/anything 一类词上。

patterns.name: 复数名词指实体或物品
patterns.context: 出现具体的复数名词，指可数物品、实体或对象；不要求固定领域。
patterns.domain: 百科、历史、法律、技术讨论

patterns.name: 价值或数量修饰的产物
patterns.context: 讨论某些有价值的东西在特定条件下是否仍会被生产。
patterns.domain: 经济或社会议题论坛讨论

patterns.name: 技术对象及其版本、模块
patterns.context: 指向某个特定版本的软件模块，并描述发布或审阅相关证明。
patterns.domain: 软件与密码学论坛讨论

patterns.name: 语义上的指称内容
patterns.context: 在解释词语含义时，用 something that is 引出被描述的对象或性质。

patterns.name: 公式中的对象或类型
patterns.context: 谈论数学公式及其关系时，泛指其中发生或出现的对象。

en.description: Primarily responds to structures asking about recommendations, processes, or conditions, especially combinations of what/how/does/should. It also responds more weakly or sporadically to hypothetical questions and generic references to events.

patterns.name: should + person + verb in questions
patterns.context: In a question introduced by an interrogative word, should is followed by a subject and verb to ask about advice, steps, timing, or what should be done; activation often concentrates on should and the adjacent interrogative structure

patterns.name: does / do question structures
patterns.context: does (and related do constructions) follows an interrogative word or subject, introducing a question about mechanisms, outcomes, or conditions

patterns.name: broken/must be degree constructions in questions
patterns.context: how introduces a question, while must and be form a judgment about degree or necessity; activation concentrates on words such as broken and must

patterns.name: Asking what valuable things would still be produced
patterns.context: what kind of is followed by a noun, and would still forms a hypothetical question; activation is concentrated on valuable things would still

patterns.name: Generic event expressions with something like that
patterns.context: Refers generically to something that may happen in the future, with something and like that used together; the passage also includes a prior prediction about “something like that happening”

9_2194.description: 主要响应疑问句中询问建议、过程或条件的结构，尤其是 what/how/does/should 等词的组合；另对假设性提问及泛指事件表达有较弱或零星响应。

patterns.name: 疑问句中的 should + 人称 + 动词
patterns.trigger: “What should I…”, “What should you…”, “How long should I…”；尤其是 should
patterns.context: 疑问词引导的问题中，should 后接主语和动词，用于询问建议、步骤、时间或应做之事；激活常集中在 should 及紧邻的疑问结构

patterns.name: 疑问句中的 does / do 提问结构
patterns.context: 疑问词或主语后出现 does（以及相关的 do 类结构），引出对机制、结果或条件的询问

patterns.name: 疑问句中的 broken/must be 程度结构
patterns.context: how 引导疑问，must 与 be 构成程度或必要性判断；激活集中在 broken、must 等词

patterns.name: 询问仍会产出的有价值事物
patterns.trigger: “what kind of valuable things would still be produced?”
patterns.context: what kind of 后接名词，would still be 构成假设性提问；激活集中在 valuable things would still

patterns.name: something like that 的泛指事件表达
patterns.context: 对未来可能发生的某事作泛指，something 与 like that 连用；该段还包含前文对“something like that happening”的预测

en.description: Activations are scattered across multiple contexts: strong points include should in questions or suggestions, that referring to prior text, and separate local uses of must, something, and mice. They are difficult to group into a single semantic pattern.

patterns.name: Questions containing should
patterns.context: Questions ask for advice, requirements, or an action to take; the context often includes what/how/where.
patterns.domain: Interview Q&A, health advice, forum questions, academic discussion

patterns.name: Demonstrative that referring to prior text
patterns.context: In explanations, discussions, or questions, that refers to a previously mentioned idea, situation, or object.

patterns.name: Obligation structure with must
patterns.context: Describes patients needing appropriate preparation during referral or transition to adult care.

patterns.name: Degree question before must be
patterns.context: Asks how badly something must be damaged to qualify for repair.

patterns.name: something as the head noun
patterns.context: Discusses addicts believing their behavior has important meaning, with something referring to the previously described behavior or thing.

patterns.name: Double-mutant mice
patterns.context: Describes experimental steps for producing mice carrying two mutations simultaneously.

9_2194.description: 激活分散在多种语境：高点包括疑问或建议结构中的 should、指代前文的 that，以及 must、something、mice 等各自独立的局部用法；难以归为单一语义模式。

patterns.name: should 所在的疑问句
patterns.context: 疑问句中询问建议、要求或应采取的行动；上下文常含 what/how/where。
patterns.domain: 采访问答、健康咨询、论坛提问、学术讨论

patterns.name: that 后的指示代词
patterns.context: 在解释、讨论或提问中，以 that 指代前文的观点、情况或对象。

patterns.name: must 后的义务情态结构
patterns.context: 描述转诊或成人照护过渡时，患者必须获得适当准备。

patterns.name: must be 前的程度疑问
patterns.context: 询问某物要达到多严重的损坏程度才满足修理条件。

patterns.name: something 作中心名词
patterns.context: 谈论成瘾者相信其行为具有重要意义，something 指代前文所述行为或事物。

patterns.name: 双重突变小鼠
patterns.context: 描述产生同时携带两种突变的小鼠的实验步骤。

en.description: Most passages activate on something generic and not yet specifically named, especially when followed by a description or a that-clause; common in forum discussions evaluating ideas, uses, and feasibility. There are also examples of things referring to opinions or topics, and an isolated pattern involving studies in a medical abstract.

patterns.name: Indefinite entity in something that constructions
patterns.context: Discusses an object, project, thing, or phenomenon that has not yet been specifically named; usually something in a main clause, also including a modifying clause introduced by something that
patterns.domain: Spoken dialogue and Hacker News forum discussions

patterns.name: Feasibility or usefulness evaluation
patterns.context: Evaluates whether an idea, website, technology, or thing is useful, popular, or commercially viable; often includes evaluative words such as useful, popular, market, and money
patterns.domain: Hacker News startup, software, and technology discussions

patterns.name: Entities in conditional or degree clauses
patterns.context: something is the subject of a clause discussing the extent to which something holds, conditions it meets, or outcomes it causes
patterns.domain: Repair Q&A; etymology and definition discussions

patterns.name: Future or hypothetical events
patterns.context: something refers to a possible event or goal that has not yet occurred or been achieved; it is governed by constructions such as seeing, happening, or enough to

patterns.name: Things someone is doing or discussing
patterns.context: things/something refers to someone's opinions or topics of personal interest, rather than a product or concrete object
patterns.domain: Comments and discussions about personal websites

patterns.name: Non-primary pattern: studies in medical papers
patterns.context: In a formal academic sentence, studies refers to subsequent research; activation is concentrated on studies and neighboring words, without the previously described something construction

9_2194.description: 多数片段激活于泛指、尚未具体命名的 something，尤其是其后带描述或 that 从句时；常见于论坛中评价构想、用途与可行性。另有 things 指观点或话题的用例，以及医学摘要中 studies 的孤立模式。

patterns.name: something that 式不定对象
patterns.trigger: “something”后接“like that”“that will look good”“very similar”“useful”等描述，或形成“something that …”结构
patterns.context: 在谈论一个尚未具体命名的对象、项目、事物或现象；多为主句中的 something，亦包括 something that 引出的修饰从句
patterns.domain: 口语对话及 HackerNews 论坛讨论

patterns.name: 可行性或用途评估
patterns.trigger: “something useful”“something popular enough”“something … becoming a big money”“something useful that has a market price”
patterns.context: 评估构想、网站、技术或事物是否有用、受欢迎、能否商业化；常出现 useful、popular、market、money 等评价词
patterns.domain: HackerNews 创业、软件、科技讨论

patterns.name: 条件或程度从句中的事物
patterns.trigger: “how broken must something be”以及“something that is so disgusting that…”
patterns.context: something 是从句主语；讨论达到何种程度、满足何种条件，或某事物造成的结果
patterns.domain: 维修问答；词源、释义讨论

patterns.name: 将来或假设中发生的事
patterns.trigger: “seeing something like that happening”“something popular enough to reach…”
patterns.context: something 指尚未发生或尚未实现的可能事件、目标；受 seeing、happening 或 enough to 等结构支配
patterns.domain: 口语推测；互联网产品讨论

patterns.name: 某人正在做或谈论的事
patterns.trigger: “seeing things this way”“writing … about something they are passionate about”
patterns.context: things/something 指人的看法或个人感兴趣的主题，而非产品或具体物件
patterns.domain: 评论、个人网站相关讨论

patterns.name: 非主模式：医学论文中的 studies
patterns.context: 正式学术句中 studies 指后续研究；激活标记集中在 studies 及邻近词，并未出现前述 something 结构

en.description: Strong activation mainly occurs when before introduces a necessary condition, approval, or subsequent action. Generic object/result words such as something, things, and anything are also highlighted, without a consistent semantic or contextual pattern.

patterns.name: Necessary conditions or prior approval after before
patterns.context: before introduces a condition that must be met before something happens or a stage begins; activation often falls on before, and in some passages extends to following words.
patterns.domain: News discussions, government regulation and legislation, research abstracts, everyday Q&A

patterns.name: Existence or attaining a possibility
patterns.context: Focuses on words referring to generic objects or outcomes, but the specific syntax and semantic conditions vary, so no common trigger can be established.
patterns.domain: Space exploration, social commentary, economic and production discussions

patterns.name: unexplained: FAA regulatory context
patterns.context: Although before appears, other highlights fall on “To have to be done for drones” and “it’s not cheap”; this may relate to prior regulation or may represent a different trigger.
patterns.domain: HackerNews, discussion of drones and FAA regulation

9_2194.description: 主要在 before 引出必要条件、审批或后续行动时强烈激活；另有泛指对象/结果词 something、things、anything 的高亮，语义和上下文并不统一。

patterns.name: before 后的必要条件或前置审批
patterns.trigger: «before»9/10，后接条件、许可或后续步骤，如“before … approval”“before … be constructed”“before … can reach its potential”“before … it can be repaired”
patterns.context: before 引出某事发生或某阶段开始之前必须满足的条件；激活常落在 before，部分段落也覆盖后续词语。
patterns.domain: 新闻讨论、政府监管与立法、科研摘要、日常问答

patterns.name: 存在或达到某种可能性
patterns.trigger: “good chance of seeing something … happening”中的«something»9；“things … would … be produced”中的«things»8、“would»9”；“don’t care about anything”中的«anything»9
patterns.context: 焦点落在泛指对象或结果的词上；但具体句法与语义条件不一致，无法确定共同触发条件。
patterns.domain: 太空探索、社会评论、经济与生产讨论

patterns.name: unexplained：FAA监管语境
patterns.context: 虽出现 before，但其余高亮分布在“To have to be done for drones”及“it’s not cheap”等部分；可能与前置监管有关，也可能是不同触发。
patterns.domain: HackerNews，关于无人机与 FAA 监管

en.concept: Uncertain events and their temporal boundaries
en.description: Activations often occur around generic things or events (things, something) and temporal-boundary constructions such as before/until. They span potential events, failures and repairs, disease progression, research conclusions, and project planning; other specific topics include drones, isotopes, and hardware comparisons.

patterns.name: Broadly unspecified objects/events
patterns.context: Refers to an unspecified phenomenon, failure, outcome, or event, especially near constructions such as “seeing,” “until,” and “must … before”
patterns.domain: Forum discussions, science interviews, academic abstracts, and business emails
