patterns.name: Temporal boundaries and event occurrence
patterns.context: Describes a state or event that must occur before another event, or continue until something happens; often linked to outcomes such as “something,” “fails,” or “damage”
patterns.domain: Technology discussions, medical papers, news, and email

patterns.name: Unknown quantity or object
patterns.context: Occurs when an object or quantity is unspecified and referred to generically; trigger positions vary across passages
patterns.domain: Engineering, aviation, medicine, and general discussion

patterns.name: Conditional questions about repair and failure
patterns.context: Asks or describes questions about damage, repair, failure, and their thresholds

patterns.name: Future expectations or judgments
patterns.context: Discusses possible future events or disease progression, often using conditional, probabilistic, or predictive language

patterns.name: Drone regulation and potential accidents
patterns.context: Mentions drones, FAA regulation, and taking control measures before potential problems occur

patterns.name: Cancer and early diagnosis
patterns.context: Notes the need to identify high-risk individuals before the disease causes significant brain damage

patterns.name: Medical conclusions not yet established
patterns.context: States that research progress or insufficient evidence does not yet permit a definite conclusion

patterns.name: Nuclear medicine isotope supply
patterns.context: News accounts mention people who need isotopes for medical testing

patterns.name: Estimating staffing needs after a project ends
patterns.context: Assumes a project stops and estimates staffing needs before replacement work becomes available

patterns.name: Price points and processor performance comparison
patterns.context: Compares CPU prices and multithreaded performance; the following sentence is truncated

9_2194.concept: 未定事态及其时间界限
9_2194.description: 激活多出现在泛指事物或事件（things、something）以及 before/until 等时间界限结构中，涵盖潜在事件、故障与维修、疾病进展、研究结论和项目规划；另有无人机、同位素及硬件比较等具体话题。

patterns.name: 广义不确定对象/事态
patterns.context: 指代未具体说明的现象、故障、结果或事件，尤其出现在“seeing”“until”“must … before”等结构附近
patterns.domain: 论坛讨论、科普访谈、学术摘要及商务邮件

patterns.name: 时间界限与事态发生
patterns.context: 描述某状态或事件必须在另一事件之前发生，或持续到某事发生；常与“something”“fails”“damage”等结果相连
patterns.domain: 科技讨论、医学论文、新闻及邮件

patterns.name: 未知数量与对象
patterns.context: 在对象或数量未明确、仅作泛指时出现；各段触发位置不一
patterns.domain: 工程、航空、医学及一般讨论

patterns.name: 修理与失效的条件问句
patterns.trigger: “How broken must something be before it can be repaired?”；“until something fails”
patterns.context: 围绕物品损坏、维修、失效及其阈值进行提问或叙述

patterns.name: 面向未来的预期或判断
patterns.trigger: “would be seeing things” “good chance of seeing something … happening” “will develop … before”
patterns.context: 讨论可能发生的未来事件或疾病进展，常有条件、概率或预测表达
patterns.domain: 论坛讨论、访谈、医学论文

patterns.name: 无人机监管与潜在事故
patterns.context: 谈及无人机、FAA监管及在潜在问题发生前采取控制措施

patterns.name: 癌症及早期诊断
patterns.context: 指出在疾病造成显著脑损伤前识别高风险个体的需求

patterns.name: 医学结论尚待确立
patterns.context: 说明研究进展或证据不足，尚不能得出确定结论

patterns.name: 核医学同位素供给
patterns.context: 新闻叙述中提到需要同位素进行医学检测的人群

patterns.name: 项目停止后的人员需求推算
patterns.context: 假设停止项目，估算人员在替代工作出现前的需求

patterns.name: 价格点与处理器性能比较
patterns.context: 比较CPU价格与多线程性能，后句被截断

en.description: Activations center on contexts involving generic referent words such as something, things, and this, especially something followed by a that-clause, similar, or a description of a property. They also cover references to abstract situations and rights issues. Contexts span forums, email, and academic text, with no unified domain or emotional stance.

patterns.name: something and its complement
patterns.context: “something” is the object being discussed, evaluated, selected, or explained; following text adds its properties, similarity, or role. Nearby words often include that, similar, and they believe.
patterns.domain: Ordinary discussion in forums, online articles, email, and academic text

patterns.name: Things as a generic referent
patterns.context: things refers generically to things, situations, or actions, with an opinion introduced by this way, a that-clause, or like; paragraph 1 also repeats seeing things this way.

patterns.name: Situation and regulatory referent
patterns.context: this summarizes the preceding drone-related issue and is followed by discussion of control and timing conditions; something/things does not appear explicitly.

patterns.name: Discussion of rights and public services
patterns.context: something is introduced by that and modified by as fundamental as this, referring to the basic-rights or public-service issue discussed earlier.
patterns.domain: Commentary on rights and public services in Scotland

9_2194.description: 激活集中于泛指对象词 something、things 及 this 的语境，尤以 something 后接 that 从句、similar 或性质描述为常见；也覆盖对抽象事态、权利问题的指称。跨论坛、邮件、学术文本，未见统一领域或情感立场。

patterns.name: something 及其补足语
patterns.trigger: “something”后接描述、关系从句或例子，如 “something that isn’t broken”“something that I can’t do myself”“something very similar”“something they believe is life affirming”
patterns.context: “something”是句中被讨论、评价、选择或解释的对象，后续内容补充其性质、相似性或作用；常见附近还有 that、similar、they believe 等。
patterns.domain: 论坛讨论、网络文章、邮件及学术文本中的普通论述

patterns.name: Things 作泛指对象
patterns.context: things 指泛泛的事物、情况或行为，并由 this way、that 从句或 like 引出观点；第1段还重复出现 seeing things this way。

patterns.name: 事态与监管对象
patterns.trigger: “get this under control before some large quadrotor …”
patterns.context: this 概括前文无人机相关问题，后接控制及时间条件；没有明确出现 something/things。

patterns.name: 权利与公共服务论述
patterns.trigger: “that something as fundamental as this can go unquestioned”
patterns.context: something 被 that 引出并由 as fundamental as this 修饰，指前文讨论的基本权利或公共服务问题。
patterns.domain: 关于苏格兰权利与公共服务的评论

en.description: Activations cluster around generic something and its follow-up descriptions, and also occur in would hypotheticals and should choice questions; the shared theme is expression about an unspecified thing or situation.

patterns.name: would in questions
patterns.context: Embedded in dialogue or a hypothetical scenario to ask what someone would do or how something would develop; passages 1 and 2 also use it for prediction or counterfactuals.

patterns.name: something referring to a generic thing
patterns.context: Refers to an unspecified thing, followed by details about its properties, use, or flaws; especially in “something very similar,” “something it doesn’t have,” “something that ...,” “something else,” and “about something ...”.
patterns.domain: Software and product discussions, reviews, personal writing

patterns.name: Questions about choosing a thing/product
patterns.context: Asks which new car to buy as part of a set of test questions.
patterns.domain: Test or Q&A text in email

9_2194.description: 激活集中在泛指事物的 something 及其后续描述，也出现在 would 假设句和 should 选择问句中；共同点是围绕未定事物或情形展开表达。

patterns.name: 疑问句中的 would
patterns.context: 嵌在对话或假设情境中，用来询问某人会怎么做或某事会如何发展；第 1、2 段也出现预测或反事实用法。
patterns.domain: 叙事、软件讨论、一般问答

patterns.name: 泛指事物的 something
patterns.trigger: «something»，常见于“something ...”及其后接描述或关系从句
patterns.context: 指尚未具体说明的事物，后续补充性质、用途或缺陷；尤其见于“something very similar”“something it doesn’t have”“something that ...”“something else”“about something ...”。
patterns.domain: 软件与产品讨论、评论、个人写作

patterns.name: 事物／产品选择问句
patterns.context: 在一组测试问题中询问应买哪种新车。
patterns.domain: 邮件中的测试或问答文本

en.description: Most passages activate after something, often followed by a that-clause, but also by an adjective, prepositional phrase, or which-clause; activation may extend into the relative clause. There is also an isolated activation on planes in an airplane-related word, and activation on as in a something as… structure.

patterns.name: something followed by a that-clause
patterns.context: The trigger is something denoting a thing, followed by a that-clause introducing a relative clause or elaboration; the clause content varies.
patterns.domain: Forum comments, technical discussions, email, and other genres

patterns.name: something followed by other elaborations
patterns.context: something is followed by an adjective, prepositional phrase, or which-clause, rather than being restricted to a that-clause.

patterns.name: something in a compound expression
patterns.context: Embedded in the rhetorical question “why fix something that isn’t broken?”

patterns.name: Word-final fragment related to airplanes
patterns.context: Occurs within “nuclear-powered airplanes,” unrelated to the neighboring sentence's something that structure.
patterns.domain: Online comments on historical and military technology

patterns.name: Unmarked expression related to something
patterns.context: something is followed by an as-adjective phrase and then a that-clause; the activation marker falls on “as,” not something.
patterns.domain: Commentary on public services and equal rights

9_2194.concept: something 及其补充说明结构
9_2194.description: 多数段在 something 后激活，常接 that 从句，也可接形容词、介词短语或 which 从句；激活点可能延伸到关系从句。另有飞机词尾 planes 的孤立激活，以及 something as…结构中 as 的激活。

patterns.name: something that 从句
patterns.context: 触发点是表示事物的 something，后接 that 引导的关系从句或补充说明；从句内容不固定
patterns.domain: 论坛评论、技术讨论、邮件等多种文体

patterns.name: something 后接其他补充成分
patterns.trigger: “something”10；后续如“very similar”“in society”“which is so natural”
patterns.context: something 后接形容词、介词短语或 which 从句，而非固定要求 that 从句

patterns.name: 复合词中的 something
patterns.context: 嵌在“why fix something that isn’t broken?”的反问中

patterns.name: 飞机相关词尾
patterns.context: 出现在“nuclear-powered airplanes”一词内，与相邻句的 something that 结构无关
patterns.domain: 历史与军事技术话题的网络评论

patterns.name: 未标记的 something 相关表达
patterns.context: something 后接 as 形容词短语，再接 that 从句；激活标记落在“as”而非 something
patterns.domain: 公共服务与平等权利评论

en.concept: English function words and modal expressions
en.description: Activations are scattered across various English function words and expressions: must, would, something, else, until, how, and a word fragment from Montenegro. Only must and would occur in two passages each, with no unified semantic or syntactic pattern overall.

patterns.name: Modal complement after must
patterns.context: Activation falls on must in predicate constructions after the subject, expressing necessary action or necessary inference; it may be followed by be, have, or another verb.

patterns.name: Questions or hypotheticals with would
patterns.context: would occurs in a question or hypothetical conditional predicate, followed by happen; passage 4 reads “What would you have done?”.

patterns.name: Description following something
patterns.context: something is an indefinite pronoun followed by similar, describing an outstanding item in an agreement.

patterns.name: Exclusion expressed with else
patterns.context: nothing else occurs in a philosophical argument, emphasizing that there is nothing else to discuss or refer to.

patterns.name: Proper-name fragment in Montenegro
patterns.context: Activation falls within the country name Montenegro, split across subwords; no clear syntactic trigger.

patterns.name: Temporal boundary with until
patterns.context: Indicates that two examination methods must be used together until whole-body MRI equipment becomes widespread; activation is strongest, but no clear pattern recurs in other passages.

patterns.name: Question introduced by how
patterns.context: “how is this happening?” introduces a question about a biological mechanism.

9_2194.concept: 英语功能词及情态表达
9_2194.description: 激活分散在多种英语功能词和表达上：must、would、something、else、until、how，以及Montenegro的分词片段；仅must和would各在两段出现，整体缺少统一语义或句法模式。

patterns.name: must 后的情态补语
patterns.trigger: « must»（第 7、10 段）；« must»« have»（第 6 段）
patterns.context: 激活落在 must，出现在主语之后、表示必要行为或必然推断的谓语结构中；前后可接 be、have 或其他动词。
patterns.domain: 邮件、技术问答、法律文本

patterns.name: would 后的疑问或假设
patterns.context: would 位于疑问句或假设性条件的谓语中，后接 happen；第 4 段为“What would you have done?”。

patterns.name: something 后的描述
patterns.context: something 用作不定代词，后接 similar，描述待办协议事项。

patterns.name: else 的排除表达
patterns.context: nothing else 出现在哲学论证中，强调除此之外别无可谈或可指涉之物。

patterns.name: Montenegro 专名片段
patterns.context: 激活落在被分词拆开的国名 Montenegro 内部；没有明显的句法触发条件。
patterns.domain: 人物列表、维基百科条目

patterns.name: until 的时间界限
patterns.context: 表示两种检查方法需要并用，直到全身 MRI 设备普及；激活强度最高，但没有与其他段重复的明显模式。

patterns.name: how 引导提问
patterns.context: how is this happening? 引出对生物机制的追问。

en.concept: Questions about the existence and properties of things
en.description: Primarily responds to questions involving something/anything/nothing/what and existence, properties, or possibility; other examples ask about the consequences of an action or the reason for a product. Paragraph 9 repeats similar text to paragraph 3 but has no marked activation token.

patterns.name: Questions about existence or feasibility
patterns.context: In questions, speculation, or explanations, emphasizes whether something exists, has a property, or is feasible; also includes the negative form “nothing else.”
patterns.domain: Mathematics Q&A, programming Q&A, general discussion, philosophical writing, business and popular-science texts

patterns.name: Specific content or reason for something
patterns.context: Questions or explanations concern the nature, consequences, reasons, or specific content of something.
patterns.domain: Technical and ethical discussions, product discussions, philosophical texts

9_2194.concept: 关于事物存在与性质的疑问
9_2194.description: 主要响应围绕 something/anything/nothing/what 的疑问与存在、性质、可能性展开；另有询问行为后果或产品理由的例子。第9段与第3段重复相近文本，但未标出激活 token。

patterns.name: 存在或可行性的疑问
patterns.trigger: “something”后接“is/that/can/else”等，或询问是否存在某物；如“something about”“something here”“something that finally showed”“anything else”“nothing else”“anything that can be done”
patterns.context: 在提问、推测或解释中，强调某事物是否存在、是否有某种性质或是否可行；也包括否定形式“nothing else”。
patterns.domain: 数学问答、编程问答、一般讨论、哲学论述、商业与科普文本

patterns.name: 某事的具体内容或原因
patterns.trigger: “what … is”“what happens”“why … better”，以及“something that just works”；如“what is this unethical?”、“what happens?”、“why ‘new is better’?”
patterns.context: 对某事的性质、后果、理由或具体内容提出问题或说明。
patterns.domain: 技术与伦理讨论、产品讨论、哲学文本

en.description: Primarily responds to word sequences carrying the core of questions and hypothetical questions, especially something/else/what/how, interrogative structures, and following clauses; topics span technology, mathematics, business, personal narratives, and lifestyle commentary rather than a single domain concept.

patterns.name: Asking whether other possibilities exist
patterns.context: States known facts, a solution, or an example, then asks what other options, explanations, or things exist; “else” and nearby interrogative structures are salient triggers.

patterns.name: Asking whether something is wrong or missing
patterns.context: The speaker is unsure about their understanding, code, or previous statement and asks whether something is wrong, omitted, or misunderstood.
patterns.domain: Q&A sites, especially programming and technical Q&A

patterns.name: Counterfactual challenge: “Why change it?”
patterns.context: First says the existing approach is not problematic, then questions the need for a fix or change; activation covers “something” and the following clause.

patterns.name: Asking what action can be taken
patterns.context: Raises a loss, problem, or concern, then asks whether there is a remedy.
patterns.domain: Popular science or discussions of health and social issues

patterns.name: Asking what one would do in a hypothetical situation
patterns.context: Describes a situation that has occurred, then invites readers to imagine what action they would take.
patterns.domain: Personal narratives, moral or social scenarios

patterns.name: Asking how an object would appear in a proof
patterns.context: Poses a hypothetical question about a mathematical object or proof method, asking what form or behavior the object would have under specific conditions.

patterns.name: Complaint about missing content or features
patterns.context: In reviewing a game or product, acknowledges that criticizing it for lacking something may be unfair, but still expresses disappointment about the missing feature.

patterns.name: Asking why a product needs added value
patterns.context: Discusses the business model of a product, tool, or service, arguing that simple, reliable, ready-to-use things are hard to sell or monetize.

9_2194.description: 主要响应疑问与假设性提问中承载问题核心的词串，尤其 something/else/what/how、疑问结构及后接从句；话题跨技术、数学、商业、个人叙事与生活评论，并非单一领域概念。

patterns.name: 询问是否存在其他可能
patterns.context: 先陈述已知事实、方案或例子，随后询问还有什么其他选项、解释或事物；“else”及其附近的疑问结构是显著触发项。

patterns.name: 询问是否有问题或遗漏
patterns.context: 说话者对自己的理解、代码或前述说法感到不确定，询问是否有某处错误、遗漏或自己没理解之处。
patterns.domain: 问答网站，尤其编程与技术问答

patterns.name: 反事实式“为什么要改”质疑
patterns.context: 先表达原有做法没有问题，再质疑修复或改动的必要性；激活覆盖“something”及后续从句。

patterns.name: 询问可以采取什么行动
patterns.trigger: “Is there anything that can be done about it?”
patterns.context: 先提出某种损失、问题或困扰，再询问是否有补救办法。
patterns.domain: 科普或健康、社会问题讨论

patterns.name: 询问假设情形下会怎么做
patterns.context: 叙述某个已发生的情境后，邀请读者设想自己会采取何种行动。
patterns.domain: 个人叙事、道德或社交情境讨论

patterns.name: 询问证明时对象会如何呈现
patterns.context: 围绕数学对象或证明方法提出假设性问题，询问对象在特定条件下的形式或表现。

patterns.name: 缺失内容或功能的抱怨
patterns.context: 评价游戏或产品时，承认批评其不具备某项内容可能不公平，但仍表达对缺失功能的失望。

patterns.name: 询问商品为何需要附加价值
patterns.context: 讨论产品、工具或服务的商业模式，认为简单可靠、开箱即用的东西不易销售或变现。

en.concept: English questions and requests for help
en.description: Primarily responds to English questions and requests for help, especially constructions such as “How would …” and “Is there something …”; also covers open questions with why/where/what and question words in longer conversational questions. A few activations fall on modal words, conjunctions, or technical explanations and do not form a stable pattern.

patterns.name: How would construction
patterns.context: Uses “How would …” to ask how to implement, present, or combine something; activation concentrates on would, though other words may also activate.

patterns.name: Is there something construction
patterns.context: The asker checks whether they have missed anything in their understanding, code, or argument; the triggering phrase does not require a specific technical topic.
patterns.domain: StackExchange Q&A; also found in general discussion

patterns.name: Open questions introduced by question words
patterns.context: Directly seeks a reason, location, definition, or explanation; overlaps with help-seeking constructions.

patterns.name: Atypical question structures
patterns.context: In longer, conversational questions or relative clauses, activation occurs near expressions of questioning or uncertainty; no single fixed phrase is involved.

patterns.name: Isolated modal or conjunction words
patterns.context: Occurs sporadically in algorithmic, specification, or mathematical contexts, without an evident shared local trigger.

9_2194.description: 主要响应英语提问和求助表达，尤其“How would …”及“Is there something …”等句式；也覆盖 why/where/what 等开放疑问，以及较长口语问题中的疑问词。少数激活落在情态词、连接词或技术说明中，不能归为稳定模式。

patterns.name: How would 句式
patterns.context: 以“How would …”提出如何实现、呈现或组合某事的问题；激活集中在 would，其他词也可能激活

patterns.name: Is there something 句式
patterns.context: 提问者检查自身理解、代码或论证是否遗漏了什么；触发短语不要求特定技术主题
patterns.domain: StackExchange 问答，也见一般讨论

patterns.name: 疑问词引出的开放问题
patterns.context: 直接寻求原因、位置、定义或解释；与求助式句型有重叠

patterns.name: 非典型疑问结构
patterns.trigger: «how» would«10»；«anything»«9» that«6» can«8» be done；«something»«9» ...« that»«6» just«7» works
patterns.context: 较长、口语化的问题或关系从句中，疑问／不确定性表达附近出现激活；并非固定单一短语

patterns.name: 孤立的情态或连接词
patterns.context: 在算法、规范说明或数学语境中零星出现，缺少明显共同局部触发条件

en.description: Activations cluster around indefinite objects such as something/anything in existential constructions with there is/is there, especially in questions expressing uncertainty or requesting help; they also occur in copyright disclaimers and related contexts asking about errors, causes, or responses.

patterns.name: Uncertain object in an existential construction
patterns.context: Uses an existential sentence to ask about something not yet identified, understood, or addressed; often accompanied by a question or conditional clause.
patterns.domain: Q&A, forum discussions, and explanatory text

patterns.name: Help-seeking questions expressing uncertainty
patterns.context: The speaker faces confusion about code, mathematics, or a phenomenon and asks whether information is missing, what is wrong, or what the cause is.
patterns.domain: StackExchange, HackerNews, and general online discussions

patterns.name: Problem statement in a legal disclaimer
patterns.context: A conditional sentence states that a copy may have a problem, appearing in copyright or liability text; the same disclaimer recurs.

patterns.name: Response to injustice or error
patterns.context: First states that an action or assumption is unfair or wrong, then asks readers how to respond.

patterns.name: Causal question introduced by “could”
patterns.context: Asks how a condition could cause an outcome in a web interaction; no “something is” construction appears.

9_2194.description: 激活集中在 something/anything 等不定对象与 there is/is there 构成的存在表达，尤其是疑惑、求助式提问；另见版权免责声明，以及追问错误、原因或应对方式的相近语境。

patterns.name: 存在结构中的不确定对象
patterns.trigger: “there is something”“there’s something”“is there anything”，以及“something … here”“anything that can be done”
patterns.context: 围绕存在句提出尚未识别、理解或处理的事物；常伴随疑问或条件语句。
patterns.domain: 问答、论坛讨论及说明性文字

patterns.name: 求助式的疑惑提问
patterns.trigger: “Is there something …?”、“Is there something I’m missing?”、“what else …?”、“How could …?”
patterns.context: 说话者面对代码、数学或现象中的困惑，询问是否遗漏信息、哪里出错或原因是什么。

patterns.name: 法律免责声明中的问题陈述
patterns.trigger: “if there is something wrong with your copy”
patterns.context: 以条件句说明副本可能有问题，处于版权声明或免责文字中；同一声明重复出现。
patterns.domain: Gutenberg 电子书前置法律说明

patterns.name: 对不公或错误的反应
patterns.context: 先陈述某种做法或假设不公、错误，再向读者征询如何反应。
patterns.domain: 个人叙事、评论性网络文字

patterns.name: “could”引出的因果疑问
patterns.trigger: “How could a rollover state cause this”
patterns.context: 针对网页交互现象追问某个状态如何造成结果；未出现“something is”句式。

en.description: Primarily responds to interrogative existence structures such as “Is there something/anything,” especially when asking whether there is a problem, omission, or solution; also occurs in discussions of unknown things, new discoveries, and things one can rely on.

patterns.name: Existential question: there something/anything
patterns.context: Asks in a question whether an explanation, problem, solution, or related thing exists; sometimes followed by qualifiers such as here, I'm missing, wrong with, or in my form.

patterns.name: Seeking something to rely on
patterns.context: In contexts of confusion, doubt, or argument, asks or asserts whether there is anything to believe in, rely on, or fear.

patterns.name: General reference to something new
patterns.context: something is used as an indefinite pronoun referring to something new that someone claims to have discovered.

patterns.name: Asking about an unknown thing or meaning
patterns.context: A question explores an unknown thing or asks for the exact meaning of a statement; does not use the fixed “Is there something” structure.

9_2194.description: 主要响应疑问式存在结构“Is there something/anything”，尤其是询问是否有问题、遗漏或解决办法；也见于对未知事物、新发现及可依凭之物的讨论。

patterns.name: 存在句疑问：there something/anything
patterns.context: 疑问句中询问是否存在某种解释、问题、办法或相关事物；有时接 here、I'm missing、wrong with、in my form 等限定语。

patterns.name: 寻找可依凭之物
patterns.context: 在困惑、怀疑或论辩语境中，追问或断言是否有可相信、可依靠或值得害怕的事物。

patterns.name: 泛指新事物
patterns.context: something 作不定代词，指某人声称发现的新事物。

patterns.name: 询问未知事物或含义
patterns.trigger: “what else is out there” / “What could be the exact meaning”
patterns.context: 疑问句探索未知事物，或询问某个表述的确切含义；不含固定的“Is there something”结构。

en.concept: The English existential construction “there is something”
en.description: Activations cluster around the English construction “there is something”: in dialogue, it raises an existential question or conjecture, followed by various complements such as anything, wrong, here, I’m missing, and to complain; topics and styles span business, programming, mathematics, social interaction, and legal text.

patterns.name: The there is something construction
patterns.context: Used to ask or conjecture whether there is an object, cause, problem, omission, or something to rely on; often followed by a modifier, with no required specific continuation.
patterns.domain: Forum Q&A, online discussions, explanatory text, and literary text

9_2194.description: 激活集中在英语构式 “there is something”：对话中以其提出存在性疑问或猜测，后接 anything、wrong、here、I’m missing、to complain 等不同补语；话题和文体跨商业、编程、数学、社交及法律文本。

patterns.name: there is something 构式
patterns.context: 在询问或推测某处是否有某物、某个原因、问题、遗漏或可依靠的东西时，常接后续限定语；不要求特定后续词。
patterns.domain: 论坛问答、网络讨论、说明文字及文学文本

en.description: Primarily responds to the “there is something/anything …” structure in questions or exploratory contexts, especially when asking whether there is an error, cause, clue, or additional content; also responds to the inquiry “what else is out there” about unknown things.

patterns.name: there is something + complement
patterns.context: In a question or interrogative expression, searches for a cause, error, clue, or additional content; common strings include “Is there something…?” or “there is something…”, also including altered word order and anything in place of something.
patterns.domain: Cross-domain: StackExchange technical support, Gutenberg disclaimers, Pile-CC popular science, HackerNews comments and casual conversation.

patterns.name: else is out there
patterns.context: In speculation or inquiry, asks about things not yet discovered or beyond view; does not use the typical “there is something” structure.
patterns.domain: HackerNews comments discussing Smalltalk technology and overlooked things in the industry.

9_2194.description: 主要响应疑问或探寻语境中的“there is something/anything …”结构，尤其是在询问是否有错误、原因、线索或额外内容；另响应“what else is out there”这一探问未知事物的表达。

patterns.name: there is something + 补语
patterns.trigger: “there is something wrong with” [1、2、6]；“there something in” [3]；“there anything that” [4]；“there is something to cling” [5]；“there something here” [7]；“there is something extra” [8]；“there something I'm missing” [9]
patterns.context: 在疑问句或疑问式表达中，搜索是否存在某个原因、错误、线索或额外内容；常见词串为“Is there something…?”或“there is something…”，但也包括语序变化和 anything 替换 something。
patterns.domain: 跨领域：StackExchange 技术求助、Gutenberg 免责声明、Pile-CC 科普、HackerNews 评论与闲聊。

patterns.name: else is out there
patterns.context: 在推测或发问的语境中，询问尚未发现、处于视线之外的事物；不含典型的“there is something”结构。
patterns.domain: HackerNews 评论，谈 Smalltalk 技术及行业中未受关注的事物。

en.concept: Asking about or referring to an unspecified matter
en.description: Primarily responds to the question structure “Is there something,” especially when asking whether there is an error, omission, clue, or workable solution; also responds to the use of something to refer to an unspecified thing.

patterns.name: “Is there something…” question form
patterns.context: Asks in a yes/no question whether something is wrong, missing, actionable, or noteworthy; often followed by here, wrong, I’m missing, that can be done, and similar phrases
patterns.domain: StackExchange technical Q&A, HackerNews discussions, and general Q&A

patterns.name: something as an indefinite reference
patterns.context: Outside the “Is there something” form, something refers to an unspecified discovery, value, ongoing event, or matter of interest
patterns.domain: HackerNews comments, user feedback, or statements

9_2194.description: 主要响应疑问结构“Is there something”，尤其是询问是否有错误、遗漏、线索或可行办法；也响应 something 指代未具体说明的事物这一用法。

patterns.name: “Is there something…”疑问句式
patterns.context: 以一般疑问句询问是否有某处出错、遗漏、可做之事或值得注意的东西；后续常接 here、wrong、I’m missing、that can be done 等
patterns.domain: StackExchange 技术问答、HackerNews 讨论及一般问答

patterns.name: something 作不定内容指代
patterns.context: 在非“Is there something”句式中，something 指尚未具体说明的发现、价值、正在发生的事或被关注的事项
patterns.domain: HackerNews 评论、用户反馈或声明

en.description: Primarily responds to “Is there(something/anything)…” in questions, especially when requesting troubleshooting, checking for omissions, or asking about differences; it also occurs in code help, seeking remedies, evidence, or additional content.

patterns.name: Existential question structure
patterns.context: Asks whether there is an omission, problem, or noteworthy thing; often paired with following content such as something, wrong, missing, or different.
patterns.domain: Q&A, forum discussions, and general explanatory prose

patterns.name: Questioning a state of affairs or one’s understanding
patterns.context: Describes code, a rule, or an opinion, then asks whether it is wrong or whether the speaker has misunderstood; some instances connect to existential questions.

patterns.name: Technical help request after a code snippet
patterns.context: After presenting code or a query problem, asks whether the implementation, form, or query contains an error; the passage often sits near code, error messages, or technical terms.

patterns.name: Asking about analogous tools or features
patterns.context: Asks whether an alternative exists for a product or service that is similar to a known tool.

patterns.name: Asking whether there is a remedy
patterns.context: States a problem and its effects, then asks whether any action can resolve it.

patterns.name: Asking about differences or additional content
patterns.context: Asks whether a category of product has any differences or whether there is extra, worthwhile content to view.

patterns.name: Seeking a reason to rely on
patterns.context: In an argument or statement of position, seeks grounds that can still be relied upon or maintained.

patterns.name: Combining uncertainty with a request for explanation
patterns.context: Describes anomalous behavior or an unknown cause, then asks whether some factor is causing the problem; overlaps with technical help-seeking.

9_2194.description: 主要响应疑问句中的“Is there(something/anything)…”，尤其在请求排查、确认是否遗漏或追问差异时；也出现在代码求助、寻求补救、依据或额外内容等语境。

patterns.name: 存在疑问句式
patterns.context: 在询问是否存在遗漏、问题或值得注意的事物；常与 something、wrong、missing、different 等后续内容搭配。
patterns.domain: 问答、论坛讨论及一般说明文

patterns.name: 对现状或理解提出疑问
patterns.trigger: “Is … wrong?”、“Is the Coding Guide wrong?”、“I don’t get”
patterns.context: 先描述代码、规则或观点，再询问其是否错误或自己是否理解有误；部分与存在疑问句式相连。

patterns.name: 代码片段后的技术求助
patterns.context: 展示代码或查询问题后，询问实现、表单或查询是否有错误；段中常紧邻代码、错误信息或技术名词。

patterns.name: 工具或功能类比询问
patterns.context: 询问某产品或服务是否存在类似于已知工具的替代品。

patterns.name: 询问是否有补救办法
patterns.trigger: “is there anything that can be done about it?”
patterns.context: 先陈述问题及其影响，再询问是否能采取措施解决。
patterns.domain: 新闻或生活类说明文字

patterns.name: 询问差异或额外内容
patterns.trigger: “Is there something different about”及“there is something extra”
patterns.context: 询问某类产品是否有不同之处，或某处是否存在额外、值得查看的内容。

patterns.name: 寻找可依凭的理由
patterns.trigger: “Surely there is something to cling on to here”
patterns.context: 在争论或立场表达中，寻求仍可依赖或坚持的依据。

patterns.name: 不确定性与求解释的组合
patterns.trigger: “I don’t know what’s happening”后接“Is there something … messing this up”
patterns.context: 描述行为异常或原因不明，再询问是否有某个因素导致问题；与技术求助模式重叠。

en.description: Activation centers on something and nearby structures, especially existential questions with there is/is there something; technical Q&A often asks about errors or omissions, while non-technical text uses it for unspecified things, discoveries, or problems.

patterns.name: Asking about a missing item or cause of an error
patterns.context: After describing code, configuration, or an operation, asks in a question for the cause of an error, an omission, or an explanation; the most salient trigger is something, often combined with there, is, wrong, or missing

patterns.name: Asking about understanding or correctness of material
patterns.context: After quoting or discussing a guide, expression, or similar material, asks whether it is wrong or whether they have misunderstood it

patterns.name: Asking whether something noteworthy exists
patterns.context: something refers to an unspecified thing, discovery, or problem; this is not a code-debugging question
patterns.domain: HackerNews comments, popular science text, and website descriptions

9_2194.description: 激活集中在 something 及其邻近结构，尤其是 there is/is there something 的存在询问；技术问答中常询问错误或遗漏，也出现在非技术文本中指未指明的事物、发现或问题。

patterns.name: 询问缺失或错误原因
patterns.trigger: “Is there something wrong”“Is there something I'm missing?”“Is there something in my form creation messing this up”“there must be something wrong”
patterns.context: 在描述代码、配置或操作后，用疑问句寻求错误原因、遗漏项或解释；最显著的触发词串是 something，常与 there、is、wrong、missing 等搭配

patterns.name: 询问对材料的理解或正确性
patterns.trigger: “Is the Coding Guide wrong?”“Is there something here that I don't get?”
patterns.context: 引用或讨论指南、表达式等内容后，询问内容是否有误或自己是否误解

patterns.name: 询问是否存在值得关注的事物
patterns.trigger: “there is something extra”“something new”“look at something”“there's something to complain about”
patterns.context: something 指未具体说明的事物、发现或问题；并非代码排错问题
patterns.domain: HackerNews 评论、科普文本及网站说明

en.concept: Asking about a problem or unknown matter
en.description: Activation is concentrated mainly on the English existential question frame “Is there something/anything…”, especially when asking whether there is a problem, omission, or workable solution. It also responds to direct questions about a problem, general references to the existence or object use of something, and “what’s going on” questions about the status of matters.

patterns.name: Asking whether a problem or omission exists
patterns.context: In English questions, often begins with Is there something/anything… and asks whether there is a problem, omission, explanation, or possible action; activation centers on the question frame and what follows it.
patterns.domain: StackExchange technical support, general Q&A; also articles about phobias

patterns.name: Assuming there is a problem and asking why
patterns.context: After describing abnormal code or API behavior, directly suspects a problem or asks what the problem is; may not use the Is there form.

patterns.name: something as an unspecified thing
patterns.context: something is used as a generic pronoun in an existential sentence or as the object of verbs such as look at; the context concerns friends, matters of interest, or ongoing events, rather than an explicit technical fault inquiry.

patterns.name: Asking about progress with “what’s going on”
patterns.context: In an informal email, uses what’s going on with to ask about the status or progress of an organization’s affairs; activation is concentrated around What’s and going on.

9_2194.description: 激活主要集中于英语中的存在式疑问框架“Is there something/anything…”，尤其用于询问是否有问题、遗漏或可行办法。也对直问 problem、泛指 something 的存在或宾语用法，以及“what’s going on”询问事务进展有响应。

patterns.name: 询问是否存在问题或遗漏
patterns.trigger: “Is there something wrong with…”, “Is there something I’m missing?”, “Is there anything that can be done…”, “Is the Coding Guide wrong? Is there something here that I don’t get?”
patterns.context: 英语疑问句中，常以 Is there something/anything… 开头，询问某处是否有问题、遗漏、解释或可采取的办法；激活集中在疑问框架及其后续内容。
patterns.domain: StackExchange 技术求助、一般问答；也见于关于恐惧症的文章

patterns.name: 认定有问题并追问原因
patterns.trigger: “There must be something wrong with the query”, “What could be the problem?”
patterns.context: 描述代码或 API 行为异常后，直接推测存在问题或询问问题所在；未必使用 Is there 句式。

patterns.name: something 表示不确定的事物
patterns.trigger: “there is something extra”, “look at something”, “something is going on”
patterns.context: something 作泛指代词，置于存在句或作为 look at 等动词的宾语；上下文是谈论朋友、关注事项或正在发生的事，并非明确的技术故障询问。
patterns.domain: HackerNews 讨论、服务承诺文本

patterns.name: what’s going on 追问进展
patterns.trigger: “What’s the hell is going on with Dominion? What’s the latest?”
patterns.context: 口语化邮件中用 what’s going on with 询问某组织事务的状况或进展；激活主要落在 What’s 及 going on 一带。

en.concept: Identifying or asking about a problem
en.description: Primarily responds to diagnostic questions containing something in technical troubleshooting contexts, especially asking what went wrong or whether something was overlooked; also responds to speculation about the cause of a system change and to mentions of additional content or issues to fix in non-technical contexts.

patterns.name: Asking what is wrong
patterns.context: After describing an abnormality in code, a circuit, or a system, asks in a question for the cause of the error; activation centers on “something,” “wrong,” “could,” and “What” in diagnostic questions.

patterns.name: Asking whether something was missed or misunderstood
patterns.context: After providing code or specification context, asks whether they overlooked something or misunderstood it; activation is prominent on “something” and the nearby “I”.

patterns.name: Asking how something happened or changed
patterns.context: Describes a change after an update and speculates about its cause; activation is strongest on “must”.

patterns.name: Additional things in everyday contexts
patterns.context: Discusses checking Facebook for new content about real-life friends; activation occurs on “something,” not in a technical troubleshooting question.

patterns.name: Pointing out something that needs fixing
patterns.context: A website has an issue, and the poster tells others they found something that needs fixing; “something” activates, with semantics close to troubleshooting but not phrased as a question.

9_2194.description: 主要响应技术排错语境中含 something 的诊断提问，尤其询问哪里出错或自己是否遗漏；也响应推测系统变化原因，以及非技术语境中指出额外内容或待修问题。

patterns.name: 询问哪里有问题
patterns.trigger: “Is there something wrong…?”、“What could be wrong…?”、“What could be the cause…?”
patterns.context: 描述代码、电路或系统出现异常后，以疑问句寻求错误原因；激活集中在问题诊断式提问中的 “something”“wrong”“could”“What”。

patterns.name: 询问是否遗漏或误解
patterns.trigger: “Is there something I’m missing?”、“Is there something here that I don’t get?”
patterns.context: 给出代码或规范背景后，询问自己是否漏掉了某处或理解有误；“something”及邻近的 “I” 激活明显。

patterns.name: 询问某事如何发生或改变
patterns.context: 叙述更新后发生变化，并推测其原因；激活在 “must” 上最强。
patterns.domain: StackExchange 技术问答，故障排查叙述

patterns.name: 日常语境中的额外事物
patterns.context: 谈到查看 Facebook 是否有关于现实生活朋友的新内容；“something”处激活，不是技术故障提问。

patterns.name: 指出需要修复的事项
patterns.context: 网站出现异常，发帖者告知众人发现了待修复的问题；“something”激活，语义与故障排查相近但不是提问。

en.description: Primarily responds to interrogative expressions that locate a problem, error, or anomaly, especially “something/wrong,” “What’s wrong,” and “What could be the problem”; it also responds to questions about omissions and remedies, as well as statements identifying an issue to fix.

patterns.name: Locating a problem in a help-seeking question
patterns.context: After describing a failure, error, or anomaly, the questioner asks what is wrong, what caused it, or requests troubleshooting help; common in StackExchange technical Q&A.
patterns.domain: Technical support, programming, and system-failure Q&A

patterns.name: Asking whether something is missing or a solution is available
patterns.context: Uses a question to explore omissions, remedies, or additional information; does not necessarily describe a specific technical error.
patterns.domain: Technical Q&A, health or social issues, everyday discussions

patterns.name: Identifying something that needs fixing
patterns.context: First reports an issue with a website or service, then identifies a problem that needs to be addressed; not a help-seeking question.
patterns.domain: HackerNews website operations or outage notices

9_2194.description: 主要响应对问题、错误或异常的疑问式定位表达，尤其是“something/wrong”“What’s wrong”“What could be the problem”；也响应询问遗漏、解决办法，以及指出待修复事项。

patterns.name: 疑问式求助中的问题定位
patterns.trigger: “What is wrong”, “What’s wrong”, “something wrong”, “What could be the problem”, “must be something wrong”
patterns.context: 提问者描述故障、错误或异常后，询问哪里出错、原因是什么，或请求帮助排查；常见于 StackExchange 技术问答。
patterns.domain: 技术支持、编程与系统故障问答

patterns.name: 询问是否遗漏或有可行办法
patterns.trigger: “Is there something I’m missing?”, “Is there anything that can be done about it?”, “there is something extra”
patterns.context: 以疑问形式探寻遗漏、解决办法或额外信息；不一定描述明确的技术错误。
patterns.domain: 技术问答、健康或社会议题、日常讨论

patterns.name: 发现需要修复之处
patterns.context: 先报告网站或服务异常，再指出需要处理的问题；不是求助式提问。
patterns.domain: HackerNews 网站运营或故障公告

en.description: Primarily responds to questions in technical Q&A formed with “What could…” or “Is there something…”, asking for causes, troubleshooting, or missing items; also includes questions about the rationale for a solution, social rhetorical questions, and “unless otherwise indicated” in patent text.

patterns.name: Questions in technical support
patterns.context: After describing a code, device, or circuit failure, asks about possible causes or problems; a common form is What could be ...?

patterns.name: Asking whether something is missing or misconfigured
patterns.context: First provides configuration, code, or problem context, then asks whether there is an error, omission, or similar tool; activation is especially concentrated on “something” and the nearby question structure.

patterns.name: Asking why one option was chosen
patterns.context: After comparing two implementations or options, asks why one was chosen.

patterns.name: Rhetorical and rationale questions in everyday social contexts
patterns.context: Uses a series of rhetorical questions to discuss everyday choices such as looking things up, using social networking sites, and following real-life friends; not technical troubleshooting.

patterns.name: Exception qualification in patent style
patterns.context: In formal patent background text, qualifies that the preceding practice or statement should not be regarded as prior art; unlike question-based help-seeking patterns.

9_2194.description: 主要响应技术问答中由“What could…”或“Is there something…”构成的求因、查错和查漏疑问句；另有方案理由提问、社交反问，以及专利文本中的“unless otherwise indicated”。

patterns.name: 技术求助中的疑问句
patterns.trigger: “What could be wrong” “What could be the cause” “What could be the problem”
patterns.context: 在描述代码、设备或电路故障后，询问可能原因或问题；常见句式为 What could be ...?

patterns.name: 询问是否遗漏或设置错误
patterns.context: 先给出配置、代码或问题背景，再询问是否有错误、遗漏或类似工具；触发尤其集中在 “something” 及其附近的疑问句结构。

patterns.name: 比较方案的理由提问
patterns.trigger: “What could be the reasons to use one”
patterns.context: 比较两种实现或方案后，询问选择其中一种的理由。

patterns.name: 日常社交中的反问与理由询问
patterns.trigger: “Why would I not” “Why would I” “there is something extra”
patterns.context: 以连续反问讨论查资料、使用社交网站和关注现实朋友等日常选择；不是技术故障求助。

patterns.name: 专利文体中的例外限定
patterns.context: 正式专利背景文字中，限定前述做法或陈述不应被视为既有方案；与问句求助模式不同。

en.concept: Asking about a problem or whether something exists
en.description: Strongly responds to English questions about problems, causes, or omissions, especially the What’s/What could and Is there something forms; also responds to there is something in statements and appears separately near unless otherwise indicated in patent disclaimers.

patterns.name: Interrogative words What’s/What could
patterns.context: Begins a question asking about a cause, problem, or new situation; usually follows a description of an error, technical problem, or background
patterns.domain: StackExchange technical Q&A and HackerNews discussions

patterns.name: Asking whether there is a problem or omission
patterns.context: Begins with Is there and asks whether something is missing or wrong in code, settings, or a form

patterns.name: Declarative use of the indefinite pronoun something
patterns.context: something appears in an existential sentence to mean an outstanding task or additional content, rather than a direct question

patterns.name: unless in patent disclaimers
patterns.context: Qualifies the applicability of a preceding statement in patent text; activation is near unless otherwise indicated

9_2194.description: 强烈响应关于问题、原因或遗漏的英语询问，尤其是 What’s/What could 与 Is there something 句式；也响应陈述中的 there is something，并单独出现在专利免责声明的 unless otherwise indicated 附近。

patterns.name: 疑问词 What’s/What could
patterns.trigger: “What’s wrong”“What could be wrong”“What could be the problem”“What’s new”
patterns.context: 疑问句开头，用来询问原因、问题或新情况；通常前接错误现象、技术问题或一段背景
patterns.domain: StackExchange 技术问答及 HackerNews 讨论

patterns.name: 询问是否有问题或遗漏
patterns.context: 以 Is there 起句，询问代码、设置或表单中是否存在遗漏或错误

patterns.name: 不定代词 something 的陈述用法
patterns.trigger: “there’s something we need to fix”“there is something extra”
patterns.context: something 出现在存在句中，表示待处理事项或额外内容，并非直接提问

patterns.name: 专利免责声明中的 unless
patterns.context: 专利文本中限定前述陈述的适用条件；激活分布在 unless otherwise indicated 附近
patterns.domain: USPTO 专利背景/法律技术文体

en.description: Primarily responds to help-seeking or problem-oriented questions: asking whether something is missing, what is wrong, whether action is possible, or speculating about a cause; also covers existential statements with there is something and unless otherwise indicated in patent disclaimers.

patterns.name: Rhetorical help request: asking whether something is missing
patterns.context: After posing a problem, asks a question with there + something + I’m… to request that others check, add information, or identify an error.

patterns.name: Asking what went wrong
patterns.context: After describing a program, logic, or code problem, directly asks where the error is; the question contains wrong.

patterns.name: Asking whether action is possible or there is a solution
patterns.context: After describing a predicament or problem, uses there + anything + can to seek a workable response.

patterns.name: Speculating about a cause with what must have happened
patterns.context: Reports a situation after an update or fix, then speculates about what may have happened earlier.

patterns.name: Existential question about something extra
patterns.context: something occurs in a there is/there’s structure, referring respectively to possible additional content or an outstanding task.

patterns.name: unless otherwise indicated in patent disclaimers
patterns.context: In legal or patent text, uses unless otherwise indicated to qualify the default interpretation; activation is concentrated on unless.

9_2194.description: 主要响应求助或问题导向疑问句：询问是否遗漏、哪里有错、能否采取措施，或推测原因；也覆盖 there is something 的存在表述及专利免责声明中的 unless otherwise indicated。

patterns.name: 反问式求助：询问是否有遗漏
patterns.trigger: “Is there something I’m missing?”（[1]、[2]）；“Is there something wrong with how I’m setting up…”（[3]）
patterns.context: 提出问题后，以 there + something + I’m… 的疑问句请求他人检查、补充或指出错误。

patterns.name: 询问哪里出了问题
patterns.trigger: “What’s wrong with my logic?”（[7]）；“What could be wrong in my Jquery code” （[10]）
patterns.context: 描述程序、逻辑或代码问题后，直接询问错误所在；疑问句包含 wrong。

patterns.name: 询问能否采取措施或是否有办法
patterns.trigger: “is there anything that can be done about it?”（[4]）；“Is there anything at-all I can do…”（[8]）
patterns.context: 先描述一种困境或问题，再用 there + anything + can 表达寻求可行应对方式。

patterns.name: 以 what must have happened 推测原因
patterns.context: 报告更新或修复后的现象，再推测此前可能发生的原因。

patterns.name: something extra 的存在询问
patterns.trigger: “there is something extra” （[1]）；“there’s something we need to fix” （[9]）
patterns.context: something 出现在 there is/there’s 结构中，分别指可能存在的额外内容或待处理事项。

patterns.name: 专利免责声明中的 unless otherwise indicated
patterns.context: 法律或专利文本中，以 unless otherwise indicated 限定默认解释；激活集中在 unless。

en.description: Activations often occur around unknown things, causes, and possible outcomes in questions or conjectures (anything, something, what, might, would); there are also special cases such as unless in patent boilerplate and questions about paper contributions, with no single lexical pattern covering all triggers.

patterns.name: Existence or possibility in questions
patterns.context: Activation often falls on a question word or a word in a question that introduces an unknown thing, cause, or possible outcome, sometimes introduced by what/there; not all questions fit.
patterns.domain: News, forum discussions, technical Q&A, and narrative

patterns.name: unless in a patent disclaimer
patterns.context: In fixed legal/patent wording, unless introduces an exception, followed by a statement about what should not be assumed; strong activation falls on unless.

patterns.name: Introductory question in a paper abstract
patterns.context: A medical paper abstract uses a question to introduce the paper’s contribution; strong activation centers on What does this paper.

patterns.name: would in a conditional-consequence sentence
patterns.context: In legal or news discussion, would introduces a possible consequence if a court takes the previously mentioned action; strong activation falls on would.

patterns.name: something introducing an object of complaint
patterns.context: A forum comment uses there’s something to introduce something to complain about; strong activation falls on something.

9_2194.description: 激活多见于疑问或推测语境中的未知事物、原因与可能结果（anything、something、what、might、would）；另有 unless 专利套语及论文贡献问句等特例，未见能覆盖全部触发形式的单一词法模式。

patterns.name: 疑问中的存在或可能性
patterns.trigger: “anything ... can be done”“there is something extra”“what on earth had happened”“What’s wrong”“what might occur”“what else is out there”
patterns.context: 激活常落在疑问词或疑问句中承接未知事物、原因、可能结果的词上，部分由 what/there 引出；并非所有疑问句都符合。
patterns.domain: 新闻、论坛讨论、技术问答与叙述

patterns.name: 专利免责声明中的 unless
patterns.context: 固定法律/专利表述中，unless 引出例外条件，随后说明不应作何假设；强激活落在 unless。

patterns.name: 论文摘要的引导性问句
patterns.context: 医学论文摘要中，以问句引出本文贡献；强激活集中在 What does this paper。

patterns.name: 条件结果句中的 would
patterns.trigger: “that would give EPIC what it originally sought”
patterns.context: 法律/新闻论述中，假设法院采取前述措施，would 引出可能后果；强激活落在 would。

patterns.name: 抱怨引出对象的 something
patterns.context: 论坛评论中以 there’s something 引出可抱怨之事；强激活落在 something。

en.concept: Introducing unknown information or an exception
en.description: Activation often occurs in questions or open-ended expressions: asking about new information, causes, solutions, or other unknown things; it also appears in narratives to signal something noteworthy and in exception qualifications in patent text. The fifth segment lacks a clear common pattern.

patterns.name: Introducing content to be explained in questions
patterns.context: An interrogative word or structure introduces an unknown situation, cause, additional information, or solution; activation often falls on “What” or words such as “anything/something.” Covers different forms and does not require a specific answer.
patterns.domain: Academic abstracts, Q&A, forum discussions, news, or general narrative

patterns.name: Open-ended expressions about something existing or happening
patterns.context: Concerns an unspecified, noteworthy, or explanatory thing or event; often occurs with something, what happened, or there is/was.
patterns.domain: Forums, narratives, and general explanatory text

patterns.name: Exception reservation in legal text
patterns.context: Uses unless otherwise indicated to qualify a preceding statement and preserve exceptions.

9_2194.description: 激活多见于疑问或开放式表达：询问新增信息、原因、办法或其他未知事物；也出现在叙述中提示某事值得注意，以及专利文本的例外限定。第5段缺乏明确共同模式。

patterns.name: 疑问句中引出待解释内容
patterns.trigger: “What does this paper add?”、“What’s wrong with my logic?”、“is there anything that can be done about it?”、“what else is out there”
patterns.context: 疑问词或疑问结构引出未知情况、原因、补充信息或解决办法，激活常落在“What”或“anything/something”等词；涵盖不同句式，不要求具体答案。
patterns.domain: 学术摘要、问答、论坛讨论、新闻或一般叙述

patterns.name: 存在或发生某事的开放式表达
patterns.trigger: “there is something extra”、“there’s something we need to fix”、“there was something special”、“had happened”
patterns.context: 围绕尚未说明、值得注意或需要解释的事物或事件；常与 something、what happened、there is/was 搭配。
patterns.domain: 论坛、叙事及一般说明性文本

patterns.name: 法律文本的例外保留措辞
patterns.context: 以 unless otherwise indicated 限定前述陈述，保留例外情况。
patterns.domain: 专利背景/法律技术文体

en.concept: Questions and introduction of unknown information
en.description: Activations are concentrated mainly in question-initial structures, especially a question word followed by a modal or auxiliary; a few declarative sentences also activate near expressions such as “what's happening” and “something extra/special.”

patterns.name: Question-initial word
patterns.context: At the start of a question or interrogative phrase; the question word is often followed by an auxiliary or copula
patterns.domain: StackExchange, HackerNews, PubMed Q&A, and general narrative

patterns.name: Modal/auxiliary in a question
patterns.context: Forms a question about a cause, possibility, or necessity after a question word
patterns.domain: Technical Q&A, academic abstract Q&A, discussion posts

patterns.name: Complement or following word in a question
patterns.context: Specifies the question, cause, or object in an interrogative sentence; trigger position varies

patterns.name: Event description following what's
patterns.context: Embedded in a declarative sentence to describe something happening; not a sentence-initial question

patterns.name: something introducing existence or specialness
patterns.context: Uses something to introduce additional information or a special property; surrounding contexts vary

patterns.name: Duplicate email sample
patterns.context: An email excerpt identical to passage 5, with the same trigger form and context

9_2194.description: 激活主要集中于疑问句起始结构，尤其疑问词后接情态或助动词；少数陈述句也在“what's happening”及“something extra/special”一类表达附近激活。

patterns.name: 疑问句起始词
patterns.context: 提问句开头或疑问短语起始处；疑问词后常接助动词或系动词

patterns.name: 疑问句中的情态/助动词
patterns.context: 疑问词之后构成询问原因、可能性或必要性的句式
patterns.domain: 技术问答、学术摘要问答、讨论帖

patterns.name: 疑问句中的补语或后续词
patterns.context: 疑问句中说明所问问题、原因或对象；触发位置不固定

patterns.name: what's 后接事件描述
patterns.context: 嵌在陈述句中，说明某事正在发生；不是句首疑问句

patterns.name: something 作存在性或特殊性引介
patterns.context: 以 something 引入额外信息或特殊性质，前后语境不同

patterns.name: 重复邮件样本
patterns.context: 与第5段内容相同的邮件片段，触发形式和上下文一致

en.description: Activation patterns are scattered: sentence-initial Because, name or proper-name fragments, formatting whitespace, and model in code paths occur separately. There is also an unclassified military readiness context from Perspectives, with no reliable common trigger feature.

patterns.name: Sentence-initial Because
patterns.context: The sentence begins with Because, followed by an explanatory clause; activation does not depend on a specific topic.

patterns.name: Names or abbreviation fragments beginning with A
patterns.context: Uppercase A appears as the initial of a name in a signature or as part of an email name string; the two examples have different contexts.

patterns.name: Utah character fragment in a proper name
patterns.context: Occurs in the place name Utah, immediately after «U»5; also appears with a report title and line break.

patterns.name: Typesetting whitespace in legal documents
patterns.context: A large span of spaces after an opinion title and before a court name; activation may be related to formatting or whitespace.

patterns.name: In-word fragment in the place name Bolivia
patterns.context: Occurs in a news headline about pyramids in Bolivia and in a location byline.

patterns.name: model in a JavaScript import path
patterns.context: At the end of an Ember import path, preceded by «data» and a slash.

patterns.name: Document-format fragment with mixed symbols and proper names
patterns.context: [4] has typesetting whitespace in a court document; [5] has the uppercase string TIWANA in a location byline. The trigger forms differ, making a common condition difficult to confirm.

9_2290.description: 激活模式分散：句首 Because、姓名或专名片段、格式空白、代码路径中的 model 等各自出现；另有未能归类的 Perspectives 军事准备语境，暂无可靠的统一触发特征。

patterns.name: Because 句首
patterns.context: 句子以 Because 开始，后接解释性从句；触发不依赖特定主题。
patterns.domain: 说明文、学术或技术文本

patterns.name: 首字母 A 的姓名或缩写片段
patterns.context: 大写 A 作为署名中的姓名首字母，或邮件姓名字符串的一部分；两例上下文不同。
patterns.domain: 书籍前置信息、电子邮件头

patterns.name: 专名中的 Utah 字符片段
patterns.context: 出现在地名 Utah 内，紧邻此前的 «U»5；也伴随报告标题及换行。

patterns.name: 法律文书中的排版空格
patterns.context: 意见书标题之后、法院名称之前的大段空格；激活可能与格式或空白有关。

patterns.name: 地名 Bolivia 的词内片段
patterns.context: 出现在玻利维亚金字塔新闻标题及地点署名中。

patterns.name: JavaScript 导入路径中的 model
patterns.context: 位于 Ember 导入语句的路径末尾，前接 «data» 和斜杠。

patterns.name: 混合符号与专名的文档格式片段
patterns.context: [4] 有法院文书排版空白；[5] 有地点署名中的大写字符串 TIWANA；触发形式并不相同，难以确认共同条件。
patterns.domain: 法律文书排版、新闻署名

en.description: Activates across various document openings: titles, bylines, court headers, email headers, and code imports; it also responds to three explanatory or contextual sentences beginning with “Because.” The commonality is weak.

patterns.name: Military operational readiness theme
patterns.context: Appears in an abstract title about resilience and military readiness.

patterns.name: Document revision marker
patterns.context: Appears in a document header composed of a report name, regional marker, and date.

patterns.name: E-book production credit and title opening
patterns.context: A book front matter page with dense line breaks and whitespace, containing a production credit and an uppercase title.

patterns.name: Court opinion header
patterns.context: A legal opinion opening formed by a date, whitespace, and the court name.

patterns.name: News headline and wire-service byline
patterns.context: A news headline followed by a location and wire-service source.

patterns.name: Explanatory sentence introduced by Because
patterns.context: Begins with Because and presents an explanatory statement about the properties of mathematical notation.

patterns.name: Causal background introduced by Because
patterns.context: Begins with Because of, giving increased quantities as the cause, followed by background on a malicious worm.

patterns.name: Disease background introduced by Because
patterns.context: Begins with a disease name and abbreviation, stating subsequent medical context or a causal relationship.

patterns.name: Email header and timestamp
patterns.context: Forwarded or quoted email header containing sender, recipient, date, and corporate address.

patterns.name: JavaScript/Ember module imports
patterns.context: ES module import statements at the start of a code file, followed by further configuration imports.

9_2290.description: 激活分布于多种文档开头：标题、署名、法院抬头、邮件头和代码导入；另对三个以“Because”引出的解释或背景句有响应。共同点较弱。

patterns.name: 军事实战准备主题
patterns.context: 出现在关于韧性、军事准备的摘要标题中。

patterns.name: 文档修订标记
patterns.context: 出现在报告名称、地区标记和日期组成的文档头部。

patterns.name: 电子书制作署名与书名起始
patterns.context: 换行和空白密集的书籍前置页，含制作人署名及大写书名。

patterns.name: 法院意见抬头
patterns.trigger: “Opinion issued November 13, 2018” “In The Court of Appeals”
patterns.context: 日期、空白排版及法院名称构成法律意见文书开头。

patterns.name: 新闻标题与通讯社署名
patterns.trigger: “Rare skeleton, jewels found in Bolivia pyramid” “TIWANAKU, Bolivia (Reuters”
patterns.context: 新闻标题后接地点和通讯社来源。

patterns.name: 以 Because 引入解释句
patterns.context: 以 Because 开头，提出关于数学符号性质的解释性陈述。

patterns.name: 以 Because 引入因果背景
patterns.context: 以 Because of 引入数量增加这一原因，后接恶意蠕虫背景。

patterns.name: 以 Because 引入疾病背景
patterns.context: 以疾病名称及缩写开头，陈述后续医学背景或因果关系。

patterns.name: 邮件头部与时间戳
patterns.context: 邮件转发或引用头部，包含发件人、收件人、日期和企业地址。

patterns.name: JavaScript/Ember 模块导入
patterns.context: 代码文件开头的 ES 模块导入语句，后续继续导入配置。

en.description: Activates broadly at paragraph openings, titles, fields, and structural boundaries across genres, including metadata, email headers, question-and-answer markers, code imports, and technical terms; some content-word activations remain difficult to explain.

patterns.name: Field or boundary markers in formatted text
patterns.context: Activations occur at line beginnings or near structural boundaries, often covering phrase openings, labels, field names, or the immediately following token; no fixed vocabulary item triggers them.
patterns.domain: Cross-domain text, commonly titles, documents, emails, Q&A, and code

patterns.name: Titles and publication metadata
patterns.context: Phrase openings and layout boundaries in titles, revision dates, publication credits, or patent technical descriptions.
patterns.domain: Webpage titles, legal documents, e-book front matter, patent background

patterns.name: Email header fields and routing information
patterns.context: Structured information in email headers, with adjacent field labels, sender/recipient identifiers, dates, and times.

patterns.name: Q&A and question-title openings
patterns.context: A question marker appears first, followed by an interrogative title introducing a specific question.

patterns.name: Code import statements and module paths
patterns.context: JavaScript/Ember import statement openings, containing module names, braces, and path separators.

patterns.name: Proper nouns or term fragments in technical text
patterns.context: Domain terms appear near sentence or phrase openings in abstracts or technical descriptions; within paragraphs, activations also extend to parts of the terms.

patterns.name: Content not adequately explained by the patterns above
patterns.context: Apart from possible effects from paragraph openings and local structure, the content words themselves are difficult to reconcile with the triggers in other paragraphs.

9_2290.concept: 文本结构边界与字段开头
9_2290.description: 激活广泛出现在多种文体的段首、标题、字段和结构边界，涵盖元数据、邮件头、问答标记、代码导入及专业术语；部分内容词激活仍难解释。

patterns.name: 格式化文本中的字段或边界标记
patterns.trigger: 段首、标题、标签或句首词，如 “Perspectives”“Utah”“Rare”“Opinion”“Produced”“Q:”“import”“Tubular shaped”“Based”；这些位置的相邻标点、换行及空格也常激活
patterns.context: 激活分布在行首或结构性边界附近，常覆盖短语开头、标签、字段名或其后紧邻 token；并非某个固定词汇触发
patterns.domain: 跨领域文本，常见于标题、文档、邮件、问答及代码

patterns.name: 标题与出版物元数据
patterns.trigger: “Utah Fishing Reports”“Revised 02-16-18”“Rare skeletons found in Bolivia pyramid”“Opinion issued November 13, 2018”“Produced by A. Light”“Tubular shaped”
patterns.context: 标题、修订日期、出版署名或专利技术描述等短语开头及其版式边界
patterns.domain: 网页标题、法律文书、电子书前页、专利背景

patterns.name: 邮件头字段和路由信息
patterns.context: 邮件头中，字段标签、发件人/收件人标识、日期与时间等结构化信息相邻出现

patterns.name: 问答与问题标题开头
patterns.context: 问答条目先出现问题标记，再以疑问式标题引出具体问题

patterns.name: 代码导入语句与模块路径
patterns.context: JavaScript/Ember 导入语句开头，包含模块名、花括号及路径分隔符

patterns.name: 专业文本中的专名或术语片段
patterns.context: 摘要或技术描述中，领域术语出现在句首/短语开头附近；段内激活也延伸到术语的组成部分
patterns.domain: 生物医学摘要、专利技术文本

patterns.name: 无法由上述模式充分解释的内容
patterns.trigger: “military readiness”及“need 2 analysts and 2 associates”中的词汇激活，除边界位置外还包含内容词
patterns.context: 除可能受段落开头及局部结构影响外，内容词本身的选择难以与其他段落的触发条件统一解释
patterns.domain: 生物医学摘要、商务邮件正文

en.description: Activation spans multiple genres, involving word-initial uppercase fragments, title line breaks and metadata, mathematical proof templates, sentence-initial Because, and a few military, medical, and patent terms. These local patterns cannot be explained by a single semantic topic.

patterns.name: Standalone uppercase letters or initial fragments at the start of English words
patterns.context: Activation falls on uppercase letters or fragments at word beginnings; some are followed immediately by lowercase word fragments, while others form place names, titles, or sentence-initial words.
patterns.domain: Mixed: reports, place names, medical terms, question prompts, etc.

patterns.name: Formatting structures in titles or document metadata
patterns.context: In structured text such as line-initial or multiline titles, version dates, and location and date fields, activation involves line breaks and adjacent title or field fragments.
patterns.domain: Web or document titles, location and date fields

patterns.name: Mathematical proof prompt
patterns.context: A StackExchange question begins with Q:, followed by a blank line and “Prove that” and a mathematical proposition; the propositions differ across examples.

patterns.name: Formula start in a mathematical proof
patterns.context: Same as the proof-question template, but the formula follows “Prove” directly; the fragment does not show that.

patterns.name: Sentence-initial Because
patterns.context: A sentence or text fragment begins with Because; what follows is either explanatory discussion or a causal clause.
patterns.domain: Popular-science/academic text, patent background, medical research abstracts

patterns.name: Military readiness and resilience phrase in a title
patterns.context: A report title describes military readiness and resilience; activation highlights military and the following phrase.
patterns.domain: PubMed abstract titles, military health or public health

patterns.name: Subword fragments within medical terms
patterns.context: Activation is distributed across multiple subword fragments of complex medical terms rather than one clearly complete word; the context mentions surgery.

patterns.name: Word fragment in a disease name
patterns.context: The disease name Crohn's Disease appears after sentence-initial Because.

patterns.name: Patent background phrase containing malicious worms
patterns.context: Malicious worms are mentioned in a causal background sentence beginning “Because of the increasing number of ...”; the positively activated token itself is not marked in the source text.

9_2290.description: 激活跨多种文体，涉及词首大写片段、标题换行和元数据、数学证明模板、Because句首，以及少数军事、医学和专利词汇；这些局部模式不能由单一语义主题解释。

patterns.name: 英文词首的独立大写字母或首字母片段
patterns.context: 激活落在词首的大写字母或大写字母片段；有些紧接着小写词片段，有些组成地名、标题或句首词。
patterns.domain: 混合：报告、地名、医学术语、问答题等

patterns.name: 标题或文档元数据中的格式结构
patterns.context: 行首或多行标题、版本日期、地点和日期等结构化文本中，激活涉及换行及其相邻的标题/字段片段。
patterns.domain: 网页报告或文档标题、地点日期字段

patterns.name: 数学证明提示语
patterns.context: StackExchange 问题以 Q: 开头，空行后出现“Prove that”并接数学命题；命题内容各段不同。

patterns.name: 数学证明中的公式起始
patterns.context: 与证明题模板相同，但公式直接跟在“Prove”后，片段未显示 that。

patterns.name: Because 句首
patterns.context: 句子或文本片段以 Because 起始；后续分别是解释性论述或原因从句。
patterns.domain: 科普/学术文本、专利背景、医学研究摘要

patterns.name: 标题中的军事准备与韧性短语
patterns.context: 报告标题中描述军事准备状态及韧性，激活突出 military 及其后续短语。
patterns.domain: PubMed 摘要标题，军事健康或公共卫生

patterns.name: 医学术语内部的词片段
patterns.context: 激活分布在复杂医学术语的多个子词片段中，而非一个明显完整词；上下文提及手术。
patterns.domain: PubMed 医学摘要，泌尿外科

patterns.name: 疾病名称中的分词片段
patterns.context: Crohn's Disease 这一疾病名称出现在句首 Because 后。

patterns.name: 包含 malicious worms 的专利背景短语
patterns.context: Because of the increasing number of ... 这一因果背景句中提到恶意蠕虫；激活片段本身在原文未标出正激活 token。

en.concept: Word beginnings in titles and structured text
en.description: Activations are scattered across corpora, favoring capitalized word beginnings or subword fragments at titles, numbered items, and formatting boundaries; they also occur in dates and times, numeric strings, proper nouns, and content words, with no single stable semantic trigger.

patterns.name: Numbers/identifiers beginning with capital letters
patterns.context: Identifiers, abbreviations, proper nouns, or word-initial fragments appear in documents or titles; the trigger is often at the start of a string, with subsequent tokens completing a word or identifier.
patterns.domain: Webpages, Q&A, email, encyclopedias, and other text

patterns.name: Titles and column-style text
patterns.context: Word beginnings in titles, subjects, or section names, often with initial capitalization and phrase-like formatting.
patterns.domain: Webpage titles, encyclopedia entries, StackExchange question titles, report titles

patterns.name: Date, time, and numeric formats
patterns.context: Dates, times, identifiers, or numeric sequences in which numbers are adjacent to punctuation, months, or time units.
patterns.domain: Webpages, email, mathematical text, and reports

patterns.name: Structural markers after sentence or formatting boundaries
patterns.context: Question markers, colons after speakers/names, or line breaks between titles and entries; activation often falls on the first token at the boundary.
patterns.domain: Q&A, encyclopedia entries, email, and list-style text

patterns.name: Mathematical number strings and variable introduction
patterns.context: A numeric sequence formed by digits and a decimal point, followed by a mathematical expression such as “Let x =”.

patterns.name: Fixed word beginnings or subword fragments
patterns.context: When a word is split into multiple tokens, the initial fragment stands out more than later affixes or endings; may also be a segmented spelling of a proper noun.

patterns.name: Topic words and entity names
patterns.context: Ordinary entities or topic words appear in section, question, abstract, or request contexts; triggers are scattered, with no consistent semantic category.
patterns.domain: News/organizations, medical abstracts, travel Q&A, email, outdoor reports

9_2290.concept: 标题与结构化文本中的词首
9_2290.description: 激活分散在多种语料中，偏向标题、编号和格式边界处的大写词首或分词片段；也出现在日期时间、数字串、专名及实体词，尚无单一稳定语义触发条件。

patterns.name: 大写字母开头的数字/编号
patterns.context: 文档或标题中出现编号、缩写、专名或词首片段；触发位置常在字符串开头，后续 token 继续拼成词或标识符
patterns.domain: 网页、问答、邮件、百科及其他文本

patterns.name: 标题与栏目式文本
patterns.trigger: «Camping Gears for Your Next Outdoor»、«Camp Shamineau»、«Flash Media Server»、«Temporary loss of passport»、«Utah Fishing Reports»
patterns.context: 标题、主题或栏目名中的词首，常伴随首字母大写及短语式排版
patterns.domain: 网页标题、百科条目、StackExchange 问题标题、报告标题

patterns.name: 日期、时间及数字格式
patterns.context: 日期、时间、编号或数字序列中，数字与标点、月份或时间单位相邻
patterns.domain: 网页、邮件、数学文本及报告

patterns.name: 句首/格式边界后的结构标记
patterns.context: 问题标记、说话人/姓名后的冒号，或标题、条目之间的换行边界；激活常落在边界处的首个 token
patterns.domain: 问答、百科条目、邮件及列表式文本

patterns.name: 数学数字串及变量引入
patterns.context: 数字与小数点构成数值序列，随后出现“Let x =”一类数学表达

patterns.name: 固定词首或分词片段
patterns.context: 一个词被拆成多个 token 时，词首片段比后续词缀或词尾更突出；也可能是专名的分段拼写

patterns.name: 主题词与实体名称
patterns.context: 普通实体或主题词出现在栏目、问题、摘要或请求语境中；触发分散，未见一致的语义类别
patterns.domain: 新闻/组织、医学摘要、旅行问答、邮件、户外报告

en.concept: Mixed symbolic tasks and local formatting features
en.description: Activation mainly occurs on Solve/Find/Expand/Factor instructions in mathematical text, line breaks and answer formatting, as well as variables, exponents, and polynomial symbols. There is also a segment of game-variable initialization code and a short text containing KEY, letter fragments, and a March date.

patterns.name: Mathematical prompts Solve/Find
patterns.context: An imperative task instruction follows a mathematical expression, or a new problem instruction appears after a preceding solution; these instruction words and their neighboring positions have positive activation.
patterns.domain: DM Mathematics problems and symbolic operations

patterns.name: Algebra problem answers and separator formatting
patterns.context: Mathematical problems are often separated by line breaks, with numerical answers or solution sets following them; these markers and some numbers show positive activation.

patterns.name: Exponential polynomials and variable symbols
patterns.context: Polynomials or algebraic expressions consist of letter variables, exponents, coefficients, and operators; variable tokens and exponent symbols are often activated.

patterns.name: Game code initialization
patterns.context: Consecutive JavaScript-style let assignment statements declare variables and set initial game attributes or resources.
patterns.domain: Github code, possibly a game script

patterns.name: Special strings and date format
patterns.context: A short sequence of strings separated by commas and punctuation, ending in a month-plus-day form; differs from the mathematical or code contexts in other segments.
patterns.domain: Pile-CC short text, specific meaning unclear

9_2290.concept: 混合符号任务与局部格式特征
9_2290.description: 主要激活数学文本中的 Solve/Find/Expand/Factor 指令、换行与答案格式，以及变量、幂次和多项式符号；另有一段游戏变量初始化代码和一段含 KEY、字母片段及 March 日期的短文本。

patterns.name: 数学提示词 Solve/Find
patterns.context: 数学表达式后接祈使式任务指令，或前面给出一个解答后出现新的题目指令；此类指令词及其邻近位置有正激活。
patterns.domain: DM Mathematics 数学题与符号运算

patterns.name: 代数题答案与分隔格式
patterns.trigger: 换行符“↵”、负号“-”、逗号“,”以及数值答案
patterns.context: 数学题之间常以换行分隔，题目后跟答案数值或解集；这些标记及部分数值呈正激活。
patterns.domain: DM Mathematics 题目—答案文本

patterns.name: 指数多项式与变量符号
patterns.context: 字母变量、幂次、系数与运算符构成的多项式或代数式；变量 token 与指数符号常被激活。

patterns.name: 游戏代码初始化
patterns.context: 连续的 JavaScript 风格 let 赋值语句中，声明变量并设置游戏属性或资源初值。
patterns.domain: Github 代码，可能是游戏脚本

patterns.name: 特殊字符串与日期样式
patterns.context: 以逗号及标点分隔的短字符串序列，末尾呈月份加日期的形式；与其他段落的数学或代码上下文不同。
patterns.domain: Pile-CC 短文本，具体语义不明

en.description: Activation often falls on internal segments of proper names, rare terms, abbreviations, compounds, and URLs. Code identifiers and boundaries also appear; the examples span domains but show no stable semantic theme.

patterns.name: Syllables within proper names
patterns.context: Strong activation falls on tokenized fragments inside proper names, URLs, or technical terms rather than consistently on complete words; some words have unusual spelling or capitalization boundaries.
patterns.domain: Mixed: email names, web URLs, scientific terminology

patterns.name: Compound words or word-initial fragments
patterns.context: Activation is concentrated on compounds, abbreviations, or in-word fragments, especially at word beginnings or internal segmentation points; this occurs in both medical text and names.

patterns.name: Identifiers and code boundaries
patterns.context: Activation occurs near class names, property names, and syntax punctuation in code, possibly favoring camelCase identifiers or list-initialization boundaries.

patterns.name: Address and date fields
patterns.context: Uppercase fields in place-name or address formats, followed by state abbreviations and dates; there is insufficient context to confirm a pattern.

patterns.name: Rare fragments in long medical terms
patterns.context: Activation occurs at internal subword boundaries in longer technical terms in biomedical passages; the surrounding text describes research or measurement equipment.

patterns.name: Titles and link text
patterns.context: A web title or news summary appears adjacent to a URL, with activation on a local fragment of the link domain; the title topics differ.

patterns.name: Inside technical compound nouns
patterns.context: In a patent technical description, activation falls on material/component names in parentheses or adjacent compound nouns.

patterns.name: Formatting/whitespace boundaries
patterns.context: Line breaks, spaces, or punctuation boundaries also show activation, but occur in a single code segment or web passage, so no independent pattern can be confirmed.

9_2290.description: 激活多落在专名、罕见术语、缩写、复合词及网址的内部切分片段，也见代码标识符和边界；跨领域但未呈现稳定语义主题。

patterns.name: 专名内部音节
patterns.context: 强激活落在专名、网址或技术术语内部的分词片段，而非稳定的完整词；部分词含不常见拼写或大小写边界。
patterns.domain: 混合：邮件人名、网页 URL、科研术语

patterns.name: 复合词或词首片段
patterns.context: 激活集中于复合词、缩写或词内片段，尤其是词首或内部切分处；在医学文本与人名中均出现。

patterns.name: 标识符与代码边界
patterns.context: 代码中类名、属性名及语法标点附近出现激活，可能偏好驼峰式标识符或列表初始化边界。

patterns.name: 地址与日期字段
patterns.context: 地名或地址样式的大写字段及其后的州缩写、日期；没有更多上下文可确认规律。

patterns.name: 医学长术语中的稀有片段
patterns.context: 生物医学段落里较长专业词的内部子词切分处激活，术语周围是科研描述或测量设备说明。

patterns.name: 标题与链接文本
patterns.context: 网页标题或新闻摘要紧邻 URL，且激活落在链接域名的局部片段；标题主题不同。

patterns.name: 技术复合名词内部
patterns.context: 专利技术说明中，激活落在括号中的材料/部件名或相邻复合名词处。

patterns.name: 格式/空白边界
patterns.context: 换行、空格或标点边界也有激活，但在单个代码段或网页段落中出现，无法确认独立规律。

en.description: Activation is scattered across numbers and identifiers, mathematical formula symbols, electricity-industry entities and formatting, and a few first-person colloquialisms and torrent-tutorial words. Numbers and formula structures are relatively common, but triggers are not fully consistent across domains.

patterns.name: Numbers, values, and identifiers
patterns.context: Activation often falls on numbers themselves, including numbers split into multiple tokens; examples include voltage, dates, times, prices, identifiers, or integers in formulas.
patterns.domain: Patents, electricity emails, mathematical and physics text

patterns.name: Formulas and mathematical-symbol structures
patterns.context: Occurs in formulas, summations, Dirac notation, function definitions, or convergence proofs; numbers and variables often alternate.
patterns.domain: StackExchange mathematical Q&A and ArXiv mathematical and physics papers

patterns.name: Electricity business data and entity names
patterns.context: Numbers, dates, time periods, amounts, or company names appear alongside voltage levels or electricity-company business records.
patterns.domain: USPTO patent background and Enron electricity-business emails

patterns.name: Colloquial first person and contractions
patterns.context: In first-person narration or questions, especially informal statements; activation mainly falls on «m», and also on standalone «I».

patterns.name: Time and currency formats in numerical lists
patterns.context: Numbers appear in time, currency, or table-field formats.
patterns.domain: Schedules and business records in Enron emails

patterns.name: Torrent-related terms in online tutorials
patterns.context: Tutorial titles and introductions contain software- or file-sharing-related terms; these are distinctive activated words beyond numbers and first-person forms.

9_2290.description: 激活分散在数字与编号、数学公式符号、电力业务实体和格式，以及少数第一人称口语和 torrent 教程词上；数字与公式结构较常见，但各领域触发并不完全统一。

patterns.name: 数字、数值与编号
patterns.context: 激活常落在数字本身，也包括数字拆分成多个 token 的情况；可以是电压、日期、时间、价格、编号或公式中的整数。
patterns.domain: 专利、电力邮件、数学与物理文本

patterns.name: 公式与数学符号结构
patterns.trigger: 数学表达式中的符号或结构，如 «\overline», «K», «\sum», «\frac», «m», «n», «\vert», «\rangle», «f_n(x)»
patterns.context: 出现在公式、求和式、狄拉克记号、函数定义或收敛证明中；数字与变量常交替出现。
patterns.domain: StackExchange 数学问答及 ArXiv 数学、物理论文

patterns.name: 电力商业数据与实体名称
patterns.trigger: «VDC», «V», «Coastal Merchant», «Heatherloch Mun», «Pringle Resources», «Shoreline Gas», «Electric Business Understanding»
patterns.context: 电压等级或电力公司业务记录旁出现数字、日期、时段、金额或公司名称。
patterns.domain: USPTO 专利背景与 Enron 电力业务邮件

patterns.name: 口语化第一人称与收缩形式
patterns.context: 第一人称叙述或提问中，尤其是非正式语句；激活主要落在 «m»，也落在独立 «I»。

patterns.name: 数字列表中的时间与金额格式
patterns.context: 数字以钟点、货币或表格字段格式出现。
patterns.domain: Enron 邮件中的日程与业务记录

patterns.name: 网络教程中的 torrent 词语
patterns.context: 教程标题和介绍语中出现软件或文件分享相关词汇；除数字及第一人称外的独特词汇激活。

en.description: Activation is distributed across in-word fragments and compounds (such as deepest, greenfield, and Stamfordia), as well as distinct words such as raw, live, repetitive, and untreated. No unified semantic or stable syntactic condition is apparent.

patterns.name: Continuation fragments after word-initial segmentation
patterns.context: Activation falls on the beginning or an internal fragment of a word; some examples show a strong segmentation effect, but the substrings are not consistent in meaning or position.

patterns.name: Premodifiers or degree expressions before nouns
patterns.context: Higher activation occasionally occurs on modifiers before nouns or on the first part of a compound; there are also counterexamples, so this is not a stable syntactic trigger.
patterns.domain: Expository text such as news, encyclopedias, business, and Q&A

patterns.name: Animal and habitat vocabulary
patterns.context: Relevant words occur in definitional sentences describing animals, plants, distribution, or ecological traits; strong activation mainly falls on live.

patterns.name: Graded readers and repetitive sentences
patterns.context: Words describing text features are activated in descriptions of beginner reading materials for children.

patterns.name: Poverty and children from minority groups
patterns.context: Discusses economic hardship and children's academic outcomes or group differences; activation involves economic status, degree, or comparative expressions.

patterns.name: Environment and green industries
patterns.context: Describes corporate environmental performance and industrial development; high activation mainly falls on the tokenized fragment of greenfield.

patterns.name: Visual impairment and consequences of untreated conditions
patterns.context: Explains childhood amblyopia, treatment, and consequences for vision; the highest activation falls on untreated.

patterns.name: Spatial scale and cosmological topics
patterns.context: A news explanation of cosmic distances, dark matter, and dark energy; notable fragments occur in distance units and astronomical terms.

patterns.name: Distinctive word forms in company or product names
patterns.context: Activation occurs near proper names, brands, or venue names, but common word-form or semantic conditions across examples are unclear.

patterns.name: Raw materials and amounts in Q&A
patterns.context: When asking about US import amounts from China and raw materials, raw is activated in adjacent fragments.

patterns.name: Tourist lodging and nature experiences
patterns.context: Describes rustic lodging and nature experiences at a resort; high activation falls on raw.

9_2290.description: 激活分布于多类主题，常落在词内分段或复合词片段（如 deepest、greenfield、Stamfordia），也涉及 raw、live、repetitive、untreated 等彼此不同的词；未见统一语义或稳定句法条件。
